text: Tower Controller described a go around event and expresses a number views concerning the interaction of other controllers in their attempt to assist and the distractions that easily result.
rewrite: The tower controller reported a go-around event, noting concerns about other controllers' interactions and the distractions that arose during their attempts to assist. The controller emphasized the challenges of maintaining situational awareness amid multiple communications. The incident occurred during the landing phase at a Class D airspace airport.

text: B747-400 Relief First Officer reported declaring an emergency and subsequent landing to deal with a low tire pressure indication in flight.
rewrite: A B747-400 Relief First Officer declared an emergency due to a low tire pressure indication during cruise. The crew initiated a diversion to the nearest suitable airport for an emergency landing. The pilot reported the situation to air traffic control and requested priority handling.

text: B757-200 flight crew reported right engine flamed out on descent. Crew declared an emergency, ran the procedure, and successfully restarted the engine.
rewrite: During descent, the B757-200 flight crew reported a right engine flameout. They declared an emergency and executed the appropriate checklist, successfully restarting the engine. The incident occurred without further complications.

text: Tower Controller described an unauthorized runway crossing event that resulted in a go around, the reports indicating similar call signs, missed read backs and minimal experience levels as contributing factors.
rewrite: Tower Controller issued a traffic advisory for an unauthorized runway crossing, prompting a go-around. The report noted similar call signs, missed read backs, and minimal pilot experience as contributing factors. No further traffic advisories were issued.

text: CRJ-200 First Officer reported loss of all fuel quantity indicators. They elected to divert to a nearby airport even as Dispatch recommended continuing to destination.
rewrite: CRJ-200 First Officer reported loss of all fuel quantity indicators. They elected to divert to a nearby airport despite Dispatch recommending continuation to the destination. The crew assessed the situation and decided diversion was the safest course of action.

text: A student pilot became NORDO in an airport traffic pattern and apparently could not see the Tower's light signal so after five missed approaches, one including an MD80 near miss, he finally landed.
rewrite: A student pilot became NORDO while in the airport traffic pattern and failed to see the Tower's light signal. After five missed approaches, including a near miss with an MD80, the pilot finally landed. The pilot executed a missed approach as instructed, continuing inbound to the missed approach point.

text: EMB170 Captain describes difficulties opening and arming the main cabin door as reported and demonstrated to him by the A Flight Attendant. Maintenance cannot improve the intermittent operation of the door and the aircraft is refused by the crew.
rewrite: EMB170 Captain reports difficulties opening and arming the main cabin door, as demonstrated by A Flight Attendant. The door exhibits intermittent operation, and maintenance has been unable to resolve the issue. The crew refuses to proceed with the flight due to the malfunction.

text: A B717 First Officer selected the VERT SPD mode in order to increase climb rate as requested by ATC, then got distracted, so that the airspeed decayed and the LOW SPEED protection engaged a which added MCT power.
rewrite: A B717 First Officer selected VERT SPD mode to increase climb rate as requested by ATC. While distracted, airspeed decayed, triggering LOW SPEED protection. The system automatically added MCT power to maintain safe flight parameters.

text: A Line Captain describes why he believes MEL 28-02-01R should have been applied to their B737-800 aircraft for an inoperative Right Center Fuel Boost Pump. Maintenance Control had applied MEL 28-02-02R. Compliance with Airworthiness Directives, AD 2002-19-52 and 2002-24-51 that superseded their Aircraft Flight Manuals was also raised.
rewrite: A Line Captain explains that MEL 28-02-01R should have been applied for an inoperative Right Center Fuel Boost Pump on their B737-800, as Maintenance Control applied MEL 28-02-02R instead. The Captain notes non-compliance with Airworthiness Directives AD 2002-19-52 and 2002-24-51, which supersede the Aircraft Flight Manual. The issue relates to fuel system operations and maintenance procedures.

text: A B757-200 First Officer reported receiving a TE FLAP DISAGREE EICAS message on final approach. A go-around was executed, procedures run, and after consulting with Operations, a diversion plan was implemented.
rewrite: A B757-200 First Officer reported a TE FLAP DISAGREE EICAS message during final approach. The crew executed a go-around, ran procedures, and after consulting with Operations, initiated a diversion plan. The situation occurred during a straight-in approach under IFR conditions.

text: A B737-800 Stabilizer Trim failed after takeoff without a failure annunciation when the circuit break popped, was reset and popped again, so the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
rewrite: A Boeing 737-800 experienced a stabilizer trim failure after takeoff without any failure annunciation. The circuit breaker popped, was reset, and popped again, prompting the flight to divert to a nearby airport. The issue occurred during the climb phase.

text: A LJ-55 flight crew suffered the partial loss of the aft left wing body fairing. Maintenance determined the failure was the result of improper sealing of the wing body fillet forward of the fairing allowing excessive internal air pressures to develop, resulting in the separation.
rewrite: A LJ-55 flight crew experienced a partial loss of the aft left wing body fairing. Maintenance identified the cause as improper sealing of the wing body fillet forward of the fairing, leading to excessive internal air pressure and subsequent separation. The incident occurred during cruise phase.

text: A pilot landed at PMP during normal Tower hours of operation and after a weather delay, thinking the Tower was closed because of its Miami Sectional posted hours, taxied for takeoff using CTAF procedures but was called by the Tower and notified they were opened until XB00 not XA00.
rewrite: A pilot landed at PMP during normal tower hours but, after a weather delay, assumed the tower was closed due to posted hours in the Miami Sectional. They taxied for takeoff using CTAF procedures. The tower then contacted the pilot, informing them operations were open until XB00, not XA00.

text: MD83 First Officer describes maintenance actions and delays that occur during preflight and pushback with the FAA observing. After pushback the flap lever becomes jammed and the aircraft returns to the gate and the flight delayed while another is sought. The times for the pushback and return to the gate were removed from the computer by the Dispatcher, much to the dismay of the reporter.
rewrite: MD83 First Officer reports maintenance actions and delays during preflight and pushback, with FAA observers present. After pushback, the flap lever became jammed, forcing the aircraft to return to the gate, causing a delay while a replacement flight was sought. The Dispatcher removed the pushback and return times from the computer, leading to frustration from the reporter.

text: An Air Carrier Captain reported executing a missed approach on the LAX 25L ILS at 1,800 FT after the glideslope failed and because the glideslope was not captured did not have the missed approach altitude set in the MCP ALT window.
rewrite: During the LAX 25L ILS approach, the captain executed a missed approach at 1,800 FT after the glideslope failed. The glideslope was not captured, so the missed approach altitude was not set in the MCP ALT window. The captain continued inbound to the missed approach point and initiated the missed approach procedure as per the chart.

text: A BE35 pilot descended to 1,500 FT before crossing the initial approach fix 2,500 FT constraint because he was using the autopilot Vertical Speed mode while managing the landing gear and monitoring LOC capture, but with glideslope capture not armed.
rewrite: A BE35 pilot descended to 1,500 FT prior to crossing the initial approach fix, which had a 2,500 FT constraint. The pilot was using autopilot Vertical Speed mode while handling landing gear and monitoring LOC capture, but glideslope capture was not armed.

text: Enroute Controller providing OJT described a confused communications event with military aircraft participating in refueling activities. The reporter noted that increased standardized of phraseology during these instances is necessary.
rewrite: An enroute controller conducting on-the-job training described a communications confusion involving military aircraft engaged in aerial refueling. The incident highlighted the need for standardized phraseology during such operations to ensure clarity and safety. The military authority assumes responsibility for separation, but communication challenges arose during the refueling procedures.
context: MILITARY AUTHORITY ASSUMES RESPONSIBILITY FOR SEPARATION OF AIRCRAFT (MARSA)

text: An International Relief Pilot addressed his inability to get required sleep in the crew rest facility of his fleet due to noises associated with cockpit door, a nearby lavatory and the release and reattachment of the cockpit security door.
rewrite: An International Relief Pilot reported difficulty obtaining required sleep in the crew rest facility due to noises from the cockpit door, a nearby lavatory, and the release and reattachment of the cockpit security door. The pilot noted these disturbances interfered with rest during the pre-flight phase. No specific operational terms or acronyms were used in the report.

text: An A310 flight crew departing SJU contacted Departure immediately after departure as directed by the narrative page of their commercially (2) provided ACONY RNAV SID procedure. Departure sent them back to the Tower to receive clearance to change frequencies.
rewrite: An A310 flight crew departing SJU contacted Departure immediately after departure as directed by the narrative page of their commercially provided ACONY RNAV SID procedure. Departure instructed them to return to Tower for clearance to change frequencies. The crew followed the SID procedure but required additional clearance before proceeding.

text: ZNY controllers described the complications of handling a lifeguard aircraft with regards to interfacility coordination and procedures. The aircraft eventually received direct routing.
rewrite: ZNY controllers faced challenges managing a lifeguard aircraft due to interfacility coordination issues. The aircraft was routed via direct procedures to bypass coordination delays. The direct routing utilized CNFs for navigation.

text: Center Controller described a chaotic situation occurring when all RADAR and Communications equipment failed during a late night shift during a moderate busy traffic period, the reporter indicating the facility's contingency plan was inadequate.
rewrite: During a moderate busy traffic period late at night, a Center Controller reported a chaotic situation when all RADAR and communications equipment failed. The facility's contingency plan was deemed inadequate, leading to significant operational disruption. The controller noted the inability to monitor or communicate with traffic, resulting in a loss of situational awareness.

text: A B737-800 encountered a mountain wave encounter that caused large airspeed and altitude excursions.
rewrite: A B737-800 experienced a mountain wave encounter while en route, resulting in significant airspeed and altitude fluctuations. The turbulence, classified as moderate to severe, led to abrupt changes in aircraft attitude and vertical speed. Pilots reported encountering clear air turbulence in the vicinity of the jet stream, with no cloud cover present.

text: A BE55 pilot became distracted dealing with engine problems which was a factor in a Class B intrusion. The engine failed completely on arrival at destination.
rewrite: A BE55 pilot became distracted while managing engine issues, contributing to a Class B airspace intrusion. The engine failed completely upon arrival at the destination, leading to an emergency situation. The pilot was unable to maintain proper separation from other traffic due to the distraction and subsequent engine failure.

text: A B-767-200 flight crew, cleared to climb to 2,000 FT MSL on a 130 degree heading after takeoff from BFI, encountered confusing and possibly erroneous pitch and thrust commands from the FMS when transitioning to VNAV and starting to clean up while climbing through 1,000 FT MSL. They transitioned to raw data and manual control of the thrust levers. They believed all pre-event programming of the FMS to have been correctly entered.
rewrite: A B-767-200 flight crew, cleared to climb to 2,000 FT MSL on a 130-degree heading after takeoff from BFI, encountered confusing and possibly erroneous pitch and thrust commands from the FMS during transition to VNAV while climbing through 1,000 FT MSL. The crew transitioned to raw data and manual control of the thrust levers. They believed all pre-event FMS programming had been correctly entered.

text: A charter crew became confused on DCA Taxiway P at K when they moved off the taxiway centerline for opposite direction traffic and then, because the P centerline was not visible, they taxied to FBO parking through the fire house area.
rewrite: A charter crew became confused on DCA Taxiway P at K when they deviated from the taxiway centerline while encountering opposite direction traffic. Due to the lack of visibility of the P centerline, they taxied through the fire house area into FBO parking without proper clearance. The incident occurred during the taxi phase, highlighting issues with taxiway centerline visibility and situational awareness.

text: The flight crew of an A310 followed the associated ECAM and APU procedures for a #2 ENGINE FUEL FILTER CLOG ECAM warning, declared an emergency and continued to their destination where they landed safely with the engine at idle.
rewrite: The flight crew of an A310 followed the associated ECAM and APU procedures for a #2 ENGINE FUEL FILTER CLOG ECAM warning, declared an emergency, and continued to their destination. The aircraft landed safely with the affected engine at idle. No flameout or torching was reported during the approach or landing.

text: MD82 Captain experiences a TAIL COMPT TEMP HIGH Light shortly after takeoff and returns to departure airport after declaring an emergency and complying with QRH procedures.
rewrite: MD82 captain observes a TAIL COMPT TEMP HIGH light shortly after takeoff, initiates an emergency declaration, and complies with QRH procedures before returning to the departure airport. The aircraft was operating under IFR, and the captain followed the required emergency protocols. The incident occurred during the initial climb phase.
context: IFR TAKEOFF MINIMUMS AND DEPARTURE PROCEDURES

text: Two MD82 flight attendants report a passenger illness at about the same time the Captain informs them of an engine malfunction requiring a diversion and emergency landing. Communication issues develop when jump seating Flight Attendant answers' calls from the Captain.
rewrite: Two MD82 flight attendants report a passenger illness while the captain informs them of an engine malfunction requiring a diversion and emergency landing. The captain attempts to communicate, but communication issues arise as a jump seating flight attendant answers the calls. The captain is unable to reach the flight attendants due to the jump seat attendant's interference.

text: Reserve Flight Attendant reports receiving a four hour call out at 5:30 pm after being on standby all day. It is soon discovered that the first duty period is a continuous duty over night with minimal time in the hotel and an early morning departure.
rewrite: Reserve Flight Attendant received a four-hour call-out at 5:30 pm after being on standby all day. The first duty period involved a continuous overnight assignment with minimal hotel time and an early morning departure. The situation was discovered shortly after the call-out.

text: An IFR pilot descending through 2,000 FT into LNS had a near miss with a departing aircraft but was never alerted about its presence until he saw it pass within 300 FT.
rewrite: An IFR pilot descending through 2,000 FT into LNS experienced a near miss with a departing aircraft. The pilot was never alerted about the departing aircraft's presence until visually observing it pass within 300 FT. No prior communication or radar advisories were provided.

text: An A300 began rolling after pushback because the Mechanic did not ask the flight crew to set the parking brake before disconnecting the tug and towbar.
rewrite: An A300 started rolling during pushback as the mechanic failed to request the flight crew to apply the parking brake prior to disconnecting the tug and towbar. The aircraft movement occurred without proper brake setting, leading to an uncontrolled rollout. The incident involved a single-piloted aircraft with the crew unaware of the brake status.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: A B757 arrived after an ETOPS flight having used seven quarts of oil in the left engine. Maintenance talked the crew into a return flight where the aircraft was taken out of service because of the continued high oil usage.
rewrite: A B757 completed an ETOPS flight and consumed seven quarts of oil in the left engine. Maintenance advised the crew to conduct a return flight, but the aircraft was subsequently taken out of service due to continued high oil consumption.

text: ZMP Controller voiced concerns regarding the functionality of ERAM equipment.
rewrite: The ZMP controller expressed concerns about the ERAM system's performance during departure control operations. The controller noted potential issues with the system's ability to manage traffic efficiently. No specific technical malfunctions were reported, but the controller emphasized the need for monitoring.

text: Air Carrier taxiing to the gate after landing BOS taxied across the hold lines for Runway 4L, the reporter listing hold line identification difficulties as one contributing factor.
rewrite: An air carrier taxiing to the gate after landing at BOS crossed the hold lines for Runway 4L. The pilot reported difficulty identifying the hold line markings, contributing to the incident. The aircraft was clear of the runway before exiting.

text: A CE550 lost cabin pressure while climbing through FL370. Attempts to control the cabin pressure were unsuccessful and an emergency descent and diversion were made.
rewrite: A CE550 experienced a loss of cabin pressure while climbing through FL370. The crew attempted to regain control but were unsuccessful. The aircraft initiated an emergency descent mode and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.

text: A CRJ-200 flight crew reported a wake encounter following an A319 after takeoff at ATL that resulted in a course deviation. Reporters suggested allowing more spacing behind A319/320 aircraft.
rewrite: A CRJ-200 flight crew reported a wake turbulence encounter following an A319 during takeoff from ATL, resulting in a course deviation. The crew indicated the aircraft was off course and requested vectors. Reporters suggested increasing spacing behind A319/320 aircraft to prevent similar incidents.

text: B737 Captain reports noting a large pressure drop during a simultaneous test of the oxygen system, although the drop is normal when one system is tested at a time. Maintenance is called and the supply valve is found to be not fully open.
rewrite: A B737 captain observes a significant pressure drop during a simultaneous oxygen system test, noting it is unusual as such drops are normal when testing one system at a time. Maintenance is summoned, and upon inspection, the supply valve is discovered to be not fully open.

text: ZTL Controller voiced concern regarding an adjacent controller allegedly 'dressing-up' a Data Block to indicate procedures were being issued/followed when in fact had not, compromising airspace integrity.
rewrite: ZTL controller expressed concern about an adjacent controller potentially falsifying a data block to show procedures were being issued or followed, when in reality they were not, risking airspace integrity. The issue involved inaccurate data block entries, which could mislead other controllers and compromise safe operations. The controller noted the potential for compromised airspace integrity due to the misleading information.

text: A pilot reported a near miss on short final to RBW after making the recommended traffic reports which were not acknowledged by the other pilot.
rewrite: A pilot reported a near miss on short final to RBW after making the recommended traffic reports, which were not acknowledged by the other pilot. The pilot had executed a short approach as instructed by ATC and was in the final phase of landing when the incident occurred. No compulsory reporting points were involved in the event.

text: A light aircraft pilot encountered severe wake turbulence while entering Washington, DC Leesburg SFRA because most aircraft use the JYO Runway 17 ILS localizer track for SFRA entry because the AML VORTAC is not available to define the areas boundaries when used with the DCA VORTAC.
rewrite: A light aircraft pilot experienced severe wake turbulence while entering Washington, DC Leesburg SFRA. The pilot used the JYO Runway 17 ILS localizer track for SFRA entry since the AML VORTAC was unavailable to define the area's boundaries when combined with the DCA VORTAC. The pilot reported turbulence due to preceding heavy aircraft.

text: C206 pilot taking off on Runway 06 at GUC reports detecting a business jet landing on Runway 24 as he is about to rotate. The takeoff is continued with a turn to the north and the reporter suggests that he may have been in error.
rewrite: A C206 pilot on takeoff Runway 06 at GUC reported detecting a business jet landing on Runway 24 as he was about to rotate. The pilot continued the takeoff with a turn to the north, noting a possible error in his observation.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: ZLA Controller described a loss of separation event noting the failure of internal coordination and less than clear shared airspace responsibilities as contributing to the occurrence.
rewrite: ZLA Controller reported a loss of separation incident caused by inadequate internal coordination and unclear airspace responsibility between controllers. The failure to follow prearranged coordination procedures led to a situation where aircraft entered restricted airspace without proper coordination. This resulted in a potential safety risk due to unestablished separation.

text: Tobago TB-10 pilot reported losing three inches off his prop blade, which caused a vibration. Pilot was in the pattern, so once runway was assured he shut down the engine and a successful landing ensued.
rewrite: Tobago TB-10 pilot experienced a three-inch prop blade loss during the traffic pattern, resulting in vibration. Upon securing the runway, the pilot feathered the propeller and shutdown the engine, leading to a successful landing. The incident occurred during the approach phase with no further complications.

text: AC690 Captain reports entering a developing thunderstorm while IMC at FL240 with no indications on Radar or Nexrad. ATC communications are lost at the same time and the reporter elects to turn 180 degrees and descend to FL210.
rewrite: AC690 Captain encountered a developing thunderstorm in IMC at FL240 with no radar or Nexrad indications. ATC communications were lost simultaneously. The pilot initiated a 180-degree turn and descended to FL210.

text: C150 pilot elects to land off airport just after takeoff when performance appears unlikely to allow the aircraft to clear obstacles ahead.
rewrite: A Cessna 150 pilot, shortly after takeoff, decides to land off-airport due to concerns about obstacle clearance. The pilot assesses that the aircraft's performance may not allow safe clearance of terrain ahead. The decision is made without ATC clearance, as the pilot determines the situation warrants an immediate landing.
context: IFR TAKEOFF MINIMUMS AND DEPARTURE PROCEDURES

text: Tower Local Controller described a potential ground conflict event when the Ground Controller failed to issue appropriate taxi instructions. The reporter claimed the Ground Controller has erred on many occasions.
rewrite: The Tower Local Controller reported a potential ground conflict due to the Ground Controller's failure to provide proper taxi instructions. The reporter indicated the Ground Controller has made similar errors on multiple prior occasions. The incident occurred during the taxi phase of the flight.

text: BOS Controller described a conflict event between two IFR departures from different runways, listed coordination failures and lack of intervention as causal factors.
rewrite: A BOS controller reported a conflict between two IFR departures from separate runways, citing coordination failures and lack of intervention as contributing factors. The controller noted that prearranged coordination procedures were not followed, leading to a potential loss of separation. No traffic advisory was issued, and the conflict was not resolved through timely intervention.

text: PCT Controller experienced a 'wake remnant' loss of separation event when passing behind an A380 vectoring departures through weather, the reporter noting the facilities dissemination of needed information is very poor.
rewrite: A PCT controller encountered a wake remnant loss of separation while vectoring departures through adverse weather. The controller noted poor dissemination of necessary information by the facilities. The event occurred during the departure phase as aircraft passed behind an A380.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: EMB-145XR flight crew reported loss of #1 hydraulic system, so after running the procedure and declaring an emergency they diverted to nearest suitable. Communications proved difficult, complicating the divert.
rewrite: EMB-145XR flight crew experienced loss of #1 hydraulic system, prompting them to run emergency procedures and declare an emergency. They diverted to the nearest suitable airport, but communications were difficult, complicating the diversion process.

text: TRACON Controller described a conflict where a VFR traffic failed to adhere to assigned VFR altitude/s.
rewrite: A TRACON controller issued a conflict alert due to a VFR aircraft deviating from assigned VFR altitude. The controller observed the transponder reply and noted the aircraft's position, indicating a potential conflict with another IFR flight. The situation required immediate action to ensure separation.

text: AS-350 helicopter, climbing through the airspace of an airport whose Tower was closed, had a near miss with a Beech aircraft in the landing pattern. The helicopter pilot had called his position on CTAF, but the other aircraft had not transmitted his intentions.
rewrite: An AS-350 helicopter was climbing through the airspace of an airport with a closed tower, having reported its position on CTAF. A Beech aircraft was in the landing pattern without transmitting intentions, resulting in a near miss. The helicopter pilot had communicated on CTAF, but the Beech pilot did not.

text: C172 pilot reports being cleared for the RNAV Runway 25 approach to 0VG from the northeast and descending to 5,400 FT prior to reaching HUXAM and switching to CTAF without informing ATC. ATC is able to correct the deviation by relaying information through another aircraft.
rewrite: C172 pilot was cleared for RNAV Runway 25 approach to 0VG from the northeast, descending to 5,400 FT prior to HUXAM and switching to CTAF without advising ATC. ATC corrected the deviation by relaying information through another aircraft using "ATC CLEARS." Pilot did not report having numbers or confirm clearance.

text: An A320 First Officer reports finding several incidents of undocumented maintenance regarding speed tape covering a bad fastener.
rewrite: The A320 First Officer reported discovering multiple instances of undocumented maintenance on the speed tape, specifically noting a faulty fastener. The issue was identified during a routine inspection prior to departure. The crew did not notify maintenance or the airline's technical department.

text: After a satisfactory takeoff configuration check, an EMB145 Master Caution and EICAS indicated SPOILER OPEN so the takeoff was rejected and the aircraft returned to the gate where it was removed from service.
rewrite: After a satisfactory takeoff configuration check, the EMB145 pilot noticed a Master Caution and EICAS indication of SPOILER OPEN, prompting the rejection of takeoff. The aircraft was returned to the gate and removed from service for further inspection.

text: An A320 Lead Flight Attendant became ill after a strong electrical smell developed in the forward galley during climb, an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
rewrite: During climb, a strong electrical smell developed in the forward galley of an A320, prompting the lead flight attendant to become ill. An emergency was declared, and the flight diverted back to the departure airport. The crew initiated a round procedure to return to the original departure airport.

text: EMB145 Captain experiences a dual pack failure at FL360 and diverts to a suitable alternate after an emergency descent with ATC approval, but without an official declaration of an emergency. The descent is through weather and moderate turbulence is encountered and the cabin altitude reaches 12,000 FT. The crew elects not to use their oxygen masks during the event.
rewrite: EMB145 Captain reported dual pack failure at FL360, initiating an emergency descent without an official emergency declaration. The descent was through weather, encountering moderate turbulence, with cabin altitude reaching 12,000 FT. The crew chose not to don oxygen masks during the event.

text: While descending in VNAV to cross ZIZZI at 16,000 FT, the flight crew of an E-145 had to manually return the aircraft to its programmed crossing restriction when the autopilot failed to capture the altitude. A known FMS software flaw, currently under review, may have been a contributing factor.
rewrite: While descending in VNAV to cross ZIZZI at 16,000 FT, the E-145 flight crew manually retracted the aircraft to the programmed crossing restriction after the autopilot failed to capture the altitude. The crew noted a known FMS software flaw, currently under review, may have contributed to the issue. The autopilot did not engage the programmed altitude as expected.

text: Hawker 850 flight crew reports exceeding 1,500 FT prior to WENTZ on RUUDY 4 departure from TEB while attempting to use VNAV with 2,000 FT set in the altitude preselect (MCP).
rewrite: Hawker 850 flight crew reported exceeding 1,500 FT prior to WENTZ on RUUDY 4 departure from TEB while attempting to use VNAV with 2,000 FT set in the altitude preselect (MCP). The crew attempted to use VNAV but encountered issues with the altitude preselect setting. The aircraft climbed above the 1,500 FT minimum safe altitude during departure.

text: A BE-20 pilot shut an engine down on approach to a Class B airport but declined to declare an emergency.
rewrite: A BE-20 pilot shut down an engine during the approach to a Class B airport but declined to declare an emergency. The pilot initiated a flameout without activating the emergency autoland system. The aircraft remained in Class B airspace, which preempted Class G airspace.

text: B747 Captain experiences confusion over an airway manual instruction concerning flight from Ankara ACC entering Nicosia ACC, that instructs not to contact Ercon when instructed to do so by Ankara.
rewrite: The B747 captain became confused regarding an airway manual instruction from Ankara ACC, which advised not to contact Ercon when instructed by Ankara. The manual specified that upon entering Nicosia ACC, the pilot should not establish contact with Ercon, despite receiving a separate instruction from Ankara to do so. This led to uncertainty about the correct communication protocol.

text: MD80 flight crew experiences loss of right engine lubricating oil at FL330 and diverts to a suitable airport after shutting down the engine and declaring an emergency.
rewrite: An MD-80 flight crew experienced a loss of right engine lubricating oil at FL330, leading to an engine shutdown. The crew declared an emergency and diverted to a suitable airport. The situation required immediate action to ensure safe landing.

text: A private pilot landed on PDK Runway 2L, exited at Taxiway F, then turned on Taxiway A where, after contacting Ground, he was admonished for entering an active taxiway prior to receiving clearance.
rewrite: A private pilot landed on PDK Runway 2L and exited at Taxiway F. He then attempted to enter Taxiway A without clearance and was advised by Ground Control that entry into an active taxiway requires prior permission. The pilot was admonished for entering the taxiway prior to receiving clearance.

text: An A319 began vibrating at about two cycles per second climbing through FL260 at M0.79 so the airspeed was slowed which decreased the vibration while the crew declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport.
rewrite: An A319 experienced vibrations at approximately two cycles per second during a cruise climb through FL260 at Mach 0.79. The crew reduced airspeed, which mitigated the vibration. They declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport.

text: An Air Carrier flight crew used the east 600 FT closed section of JNU Runway 8/26 as part of the takeoff runway because the runway closure makings, lights and barricades did not clearly define the usable beginning of Runway 26.
rewrite: The flight crew of an Air Carrier used the east 600 FT closed section of JNU Runway 8/26 for takeoff, as the runway closure markings, lights, and barricades failed to clearly define the usable threshold of Runway 26. The crew proceeded without proper visual cues, relying on the absence of runway status lights and displaced threshold indicators to determine the active runway configuration.

text: MD80 Captain experiences a loss of cabin pressurization at FL310 shortly after level off. QRH procedures, including manual closing of the outflow valve are unsuccessful and an emergency descent is initiated. Flight returns to departure airport. Cabin altitude remains below 11,000 FT and masks do not drop but Flight Attendant's report personally using oxygen bottles on their own initiative.
rewrite: MD80 captain experiences a loss of cabin pressurization at FL310 shortly after leveling off. QRH procedures, including manual closure of the outflow valve, fail to resolve the issue, prompting an emergency descent mode activation. The flight returns to the departure airport with cabin altitude remaining below 11,000 FT; masks do not deploy, but the flight attendant reports using oxygen bottles on their own initiative.

text: A Falcon 900 autopilot failed to capture 1,500 FT on the TEB RUUDY 4 SID so the Captain disconnected the autopilot and manually returned to the SID altitude constraint.
rewrite: The Falcon 900's autopilot failed to capture the 1,500 FT altitude restriction on the TEB RUUDY 4 SID. The Captain disengaged the autopilot and manually adjusted the aircraft to meet the SID altitude constraint. The autopilot did not properly follow the published altitude restriction during the en route transition segment.

text: PCT Controller voiced concern regarding the thirty degree intercept rule during Visual Approach procedures noting BWI with one downwind does not benefit from the new requirements.
rewrite: During a Visual Approach procedure, the PCT controller expressed concern about the thirty-degree intercept rule, noting that BWI with one downwind does not benefit from the new requirements. The controller highlighted the potential safety implications of not adhering to the updated intercept guidelines during visual flight operations.

text: G450 First Officer reports overshooting the 1,500 FT initial level off altitude on the RUUDY4 departure from TEB. The autopilot was engaged at 900 FT and was unable to make to make the level off precisely.
rewrite: During the RUUDY4 departure from TEB, the G450 First Officer reported overshooting the 1,500 FT initial level off altitude. The autopilot was engaged at 900 FT and failed to achieve a precise level off, resulting in an overshoot. The aircraft continued past the assigned altitude during the climb phase.

text: SR22 pilot reports inadvertently entering a TFR for a sports event. DET Tower had issued an advisory prior to TFR entry then issued instructions to exit quickly. The TFR was not included in the preflight briefing and did not show up on the moving map display.
rewrite: A SR22 pilot inadvertently entered a TFR for a sports event without prior awareness. DET Tower issued a VFR NOT RECOMMENDED advisory before the entry and instructed the pilot to exit quickly. The TFR was not included in the preflight briefing and did not appear on the moving map display.

text: C525 Captain approaching WENTZ at 1,500 FT (RUUDY 4 from TEB) attempts to engage the autopilot without success. During this time the altitude drifts up to 1,700 FT prior to WENTZ and is corrected back to 1,500 FT, but TASCA is crossed at 1,500 FT instead of the 2,000 FT published.
rewrite: C525 Captain approaching WENTZ at 1,500 FT (RUUDY 4 from TEB) attempts to engage the autopilot without success. Altitude drifts up to 1,700 FT before WENTZ, then is corrected back to 1,500 FT. However, TASCA is crossed at 1,500 FT instead of the published 2,000 FT OROCA.

text: C172 instructor reports a NMAC at 5,000 FT during vectors for an ILS approach at Asheville, with an RV-8 that had been pointed out by ATC.
rewrite: During vectors for an ILS approach at Asheville, a C172 instructor reported a near mid-air collision (NMAC) at 5,000 FT with an RV-8 that ATC had previously pointed out. The instructor was conducting a touch-and-go landing, and the RV-8 was on a parallel course. The NMAC occurred while the C172 was in the approach gate, approximately 5 miles from the final approach fix.

text: An air carrier Captain reported that the CLT Runway 5 ILS glide slope has significant fluctuations especially near KECKS.
rewrite: An air carrier captain reported significant glide slope fluctuations on CLT Runway 5 ILS, particularly near KECKS, affecting approach stability. The variations were noted during the final approach phase, impacting the glide path and requiring adjustments. The captain observed inconsistent glide slope indications, posing challenges for maintaining the correct descent profile.

text: An A321 Flight Attendant crew reported a foul smelling odor and, after consulting with Maintenance, the #2 pack was secured. Then the flight descended to 10,000 feet and with both Packs OFF finally diverted to a nearby airport, where the flight attendants sought medical treatment.
rewrite: A foul-smelling odor was reported by the flight attendant crew on an A321. After consulting with maintenance, the #2 pack was secured. The flight descended to 10,000 feet with both packs off and diverted to a nearby airport for medical treatment.

text: A CRJ-200 Captain reported his continued concerns regarding the complexity of Optimized Descent Profiles into MEM and contributed a proposed flight crew do's and don'ts checklist to simplify compliance.
rewrite: A CRJ-200 Captain expressed continued concerns about the complexity of Optimized Descent Profiles into MEM and submitted a proposed flight crew do's and don'ts checklist to simplify compliance with the procedures. The pilot emphasized the need for clearer guidance during the profile descent phase to ensure safe and consistent execution. The checklist aimed to address common errors and enhance situational awareness during the descent.

text: A C172 Flight Instructor reported loss of power when carburetor heat apparently was unable to cope with the icing conditions. Aircraft diverted to a nearby military airfield.
rewrite: A C172 flight instructor experienced a flameout due to carburetor ice, which carburetor heat could not mitigate. The aircraft diverted to a nearby military airfield. The instructor reported the loss of power during the approach phase.

text: Air carrier Captain reported hazardous ramp conditions at JAN at night because of poor taxiway markings and ramp lighting.
rewrite: An air carrier captain reported hazardous ramp conditions at JAN during nighttime operations due to poor taxiway markings and inadequate ramp lighting, affecting situational awareness and taxi maneuvering. The nonmovement areas, including the ramp and taxiways, were not adequately illuminated, increasing the risk of runway incursions and operational errors.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: An MD-80 Captain described concerns regarding the implementation of complex optimized descent procedures into DCA and STL, stressing the concurrent removal of previously active STARs which were compatible with his fleet's autoflight/FMS capabilities, the result of which places excessive demands on the flight crew.
rewrite: An MD-80 Captain expressed concerns about implementing complex optimized descent procedures into DCA and STL, noting the concurrent removal of previously active STARs compatible with his fleet's autoflight and FMS systems. This change increases crew workload and places excessive demands on the flight crew during the en route descent phase.

text: C90 Controller described an alleged wake turbulence separation event when climbing one aircraft through a point in space that had recently been occupied by a 'heavy' jet.
rewrite: A Cessna 172 was climbing through a point in space directly behind a heavy jet, leading the controller to report an alleged wake turbulence separation event. The heavy jet had recently occupied the area, raising concerns about potential wake turbulence effects on the following aircraft. The controller noted the C90's position relative to the heavy jet's previous flight path.

text: A Corporate Jet crew reported the aircraft's FMS crossing altitudes and airspeed constraints for the APA DUNNN1 Arrival are incorrect at LAYLA, DUNNN and IMAGN.
rewrite: A Corporate Jet crew reported incorrect FMS crossing altitudes and airspeed constraints for the APA DUNNN1 Arrival at LAYLA, DUNNN, and IMAGN. The crew noted discrepancies in the programmed altitudes and speed restrictions, which did not align with the published arrival procedures. The FMS did not correctly apply the required altitude constraints at these fixes.

text: A320 flight crew experiences a gradual loss of cabin pressurization during initial descent for landing with the First Officer the pilot flying. ECAM actions are complied with when cabin altitude exceeds 10,000 feet and manual pressurization is attempted. At one point during descent, aircraft began to over pressurize and safety valve opens. Flight continues to destination for normal landing and during taxi in ECAM alerts to cabin being pressurized on the ground.
rewrite: During the initial descent, the A320 flight crew encountered a gradual loss of cabin pressurization. The First Officer was pilot flying, and ECAM procedures were followed when cabin altitude exceeded 10,000 feet. The aircraft experienced over-pressurization, triggering the safety valve, and the flight continued to the destination for a normal landing, with ECAM alerts indicating pressurization on the ground during taxi.

text: C182 pilot reports a total electrical failure in IMC at night over mountainous terrain. With ATC assistance the reporter is able to land safely.
rewrite: A Cessna 182 pilot experienced a total electrical failure in instrument meteorological conditions at night over mountainous terrain. With ATC assistance, the pilot was able to navigate and land safely. The pilot reported the emergency and followed ATC instructions to ensure a successful outcome.

text: B737-800 First Officer reported autopilot dropped out of VNAV and started a sharp descent on two occasions.
rewrite: During the approach phase, the B737-800's autopilot disengaged from VNAV, resulting in two instances of abrupt descent. The First Officer noted the loss of vertical navigation guidance and initiated a manual descent. The aircraft experienced uncommanded speed adjustments as the autopilot failed to maintain the programmed descent profile.

text: ZAU Controller voiced concern regarding an ERAM dropped data block, recommending a return to the HOST RADAR system.
rewrite: The ZAU controller expressed concern about an ERAM dropped data block, noting the associated radar target had lost its data block. The controller recommended reverting to the host radar system for accurate identification and altitude information. The situation involved a potential loss of automated information transfer, impacting radar coordination.

text: K90 Controller suggested utilization of the ASR-9 RADAR system in lieu of CENRAP operations when the ASR-8 RADAR system is scheduled out of service, noting the ASR-9 operation maintains a higher degree of safety.
rewrite: The K90 Controller recommended using the ASR-9 Radar System instead of CENRAP due to the ASR-8 being out of service, stating that ASR-9 provides a safer operational environment. The controller emphasized the enhanced safety margins offered by ASR-9, which maintains proper target resolution and utilizes GEO MAP for accurate situational awareness.

text: Air Carrier pilot voiced concern regarding the FAA's failure to re-certify the ILS CAT II/III ILS system at BWI after runway maintenance had been completed, noting the significant disruption caused by this event.
rewrite: An air carrier pilot expressed concern over the FAA's delay in re-certifying the ILS CAT II/III system at BWI following runway maintenance, highlighting the operational disruption caused by the unavailability of the approach system. The pilot noted the impact on flight operations and the need for timely re-certification to ensure safe and efficient arrivals. The issue arose after maintenance work was completed, leaving the facility without a certified ILS system for an extended period.

text: CE750 flight crew reports apparently accepting a clearance for another flight departing TEB on the RUUDY 4 departure and starting a climb to 6,000 FT direct to ELVAE.
rewrite: CE750 flight crew accepted a clearance for another flight departing TEB on the RUUDY 4 departure, initiating a climb to 6,000 FT direct to ELVAE. The crew reportedly acknowledged the clearance and began climbing without further clarification. The situation involved a potential miscommunication or error in accepting an incorrect departure clearance.
context: CLEARANCE VOID IF NOT OFF BY (TIME)

text: A Maintenance Quality Assurance Manager for a Cargo Operator report the lack of updated information in Cessna's 208 Series Airframe Illustrated Parts Catalog (IPC), Service Bulletins, Avionics Installation Manual and Wiring Manuals. Data from 1997 for Avionics Master Switches, CM3589-30, still had not been incorporated in the revised 2011 IPC Manual resulting in an incorrect part installation.
rewrite: A Maintenance Quality Assurance Manager for a Cargo Operator reported that the Cessna 208 Series Airframe Illustrated Parts Catalog (IPC), Service Bulletins, Avionics Installation Manual, and Wiring Manuals lacked updated information. Data from 1997 regarding Avionics Master Switches, model CM3589-30, was not incorporated into the revised 2011 IPC Manual, leading to incorrect part installations.

text: A300-600 flight crew reported failure of pitch trim system in cruise flight at FL320. Running procedure did not help, and the flight diverted to a nearby suitable airport.
rewrite: During cruise at FL320, the A300-600 flight crew experienced a pitch trim system failure. Attempts to run the procedure were unsuccessful, leading to a diversion to a nearby suitable airport. The issue occurred during the climbout phase after takeoff.

text: ZOB Controller voiced concern regarding N90's manipulation of TBFM data with incorrect runway configuration data causing the need for delay vectoring in close proximity to airspace borders, indicating TBFM actions should be confined to ARTCC's.
rewrite: ZOB controller expressed concern about N90's incorrect runway configuration data affecting TBFM data, leading to delay vectoring near airspace borders. The controller indicated TBFM actions should be limited to ARTCC, as the manipulation impacted traffic flow and required manual intervention. The issue involved inaccurate aircraft list entries affecting meter reference point data.

text: P180 First Officer reports a track deviation during the TEB8 from TEB resulting in a late turn to the 280 degree heading. A power interruption had occurred after the first engine start due to the battery not being connected, which apparently affected the FMC.
rewrite: During the TEB8 approach from TEB, the First Officer reported a track deviation requiring a late turn to heading 280 degrees. A power interruption occurred after the first engine start due to the battery not being connected, affecting the FMC. The pilot was instructed to fly heading 280 degrees to maintain the approach path.

text: B767 flight crew experiences a TE flap disagree EICAS message when the flaps are selected to 25 degeees during approach. A go-around is initiated and the QRH is consulted, resulting in a landing at the current flap setting.
rewrite: During the approach phase, a B767 flight crew encountered a TE flap disagree EICAS message while selecting flaps to 25 degrees. The crew initiated a go-around and consulted the QRH. The aircraft eventually landed with the flaps set at 25 degrees.

text: A Flight Attendant reported that the slides on door 1 left and 1 right on the B777 had been disarmed upon arrival. A Maintenance Technician that rode the brakes during the tow from the gate to the hanger mistook the slide has disarmed in the dark cabin and opened the door, deploying the slide.
rewrite: A maintenance technician, riding the brakes during tow from the gate to the hanger, disarmed the slides on door 1L and 1R on the B777, mistaking the slide disarm status in the dark cabin. This led to the deployment of the slides when the doors were opened upon arrival. The flight attendant noted the slides were disarmed upon arrival.

text: Gulfstream V corporate flight crew deviated from departure procedure. Captain stated distraction dealing with First Officer climb rate was a contributor to the incident.
rewrite: Gulfstream V crew deviated from the departure procedure. The captain cited distraction from the first officer's climb rate as a contributing factor. The deviation involved an off-course maneuver to avoid turbulence.

text: Beechcraft Baron pilot shut down the left engine due to low oil pressure indication and returned to departure airport.
rewrite: A Beechcraft Baron pilot shut down the left engine after a low oil pressure indication during cruise. The pilot initiated a return to the departure airport, following standard procedures for engine failure. No emergency autoland system was activated.

text: A B737 flight crew failed to comply with the crossing restriction departing ABQ on the MNZNO RNAV SID. Task saturation by the hand flying pilot flying and failure of the pilot not flying to reengage VNAV after complying with restrictions at YUGLU were cited as major contributing factors.
rewrite: A B737 flight crew failed to comply with the crossing restriction at ABQ on the MNZNO RNAV SID. The pilot flying was overwhelmed by task saturation while hand-flying, and the pilot not flying did not reengage VNAV after complying with restrictions at YUGLU. This contributed to the deviation from the published procedure.

text: After rejecting a takeoff because of a 'Wheel not turning' warning the flight crew of an MD-80 was further surprised when, at the gate prior to deplaning passengers, the aircraft rolled backwards striking the jetway with an open entry door despite having had the nose wheel chocked by a ground crewman.
rewrite: After rejecting takeoff due to a 'Wheel not turning' warning, the MD-80 flight crew was surprised when, at the gate, the aircraft rolled backward, striking the jetway with an open entry door, despite the nose wheel being chocked by ground crew.
context: VERIFY SPECIFIC DIRECTION OF TAKEOFF (OR TURNS AFTER TAKEOFF)

text: Attempting to create a way point to comply with an ATC crossing restriction, the waypoint created using place/bearing/distance does not fall precisely on the direct route but is accepted by the crew. ATC questions the deviation and the crew proceeds direct.
rewrite: The crew attempted to create a waypoint to comply with an ATC crossing restriction, using place/bearing/distance, but the waypoint did not align precisely with the direct route. ATC questioned the deviation, and the crew proceeded direct to meet the crossing restriction.

text: MD-82 had unsafe gear indication, declared an emergency, accomplished uneventful landing.
rewrite: MD-82 experienced an unsafe gear indication during the final approach segment, prompting the pilot to declare a minimum fuel emergency. The crew managed to complete an uneventful landing with no further issues reported. The landing distance available was sufficient for the aircraft's landing requirements.

text: A320 flight crew experiences an apparent pressurization anomaly after commencing descent and receives clearance for an expedited descent to 10,000 feet. The cabin pressure indication eventually rises to 14,500 feet where the passenger oxygen masks are automatically deployed. Attempts to control the cabin pressure manually are not successful with the safety valve opening at one point, indicating a cabin over pressure.
rewrite: An A320 flight crew encountered a pressurization anomaly during descent after being cleared for an expedited descent to 10,000 feet. Cabin pressure climbed to 14,500 feet, triggering automatic deployment of passenger oxygen masks. Manual control efforts failed, and the safety valve opened, indicating cabin overpressure.

text: ZSE Controller expressed concern regarding ERAM problems that resurfaced after recent software re-build.
rewrite: ZSE Controller reported recurring ERAM system issues following a recent software rebuild, affecting the timely implementation of airborne reroutes and adapted routes. The controller noted operational disruptions during traffic flow management, impacting radar services and flight plan coordination. Concerns were raised about the system's reliability and its effect on controller workload and airspace management.

text: C340 pilot experienced an engine failure shortly after leveling off at 10,000 FT. An emergency is declared and flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport. The pilot reports difficulty managing the emergency and flying the single engine ILS in IMC and turbulence as a single pilot. The gear is extended early resulting in difficulty maintaining approach speed.
rewrite: A C-340 pilot experienced an engine failure shortly after leveling off at 10,000 feet. An emergency was declared, and the flight diverted to the nearest suitable airport. As a single-piloted aircraft, the pilot reported difficulty managing the emergency, flying the single-engine ILS in IMC, and maintaining approach speed due to early gear extension and turbulence.

text: B767-300 Flight Attendant identified multiple safety equipment and safety check issues.
rewrite: A flight attendant on a B767-300 identified multiple safety equipment and safety check issues during the pre-flight inspection. The crew noted deficiencies in emergency equipment, including missing fire extinguishers and improperly secured oxygen masks. These issues were reported to the captain for further action.

text: The flight crew of an A320 noted excessive vibration in the left engine during taxi out after being de and anti-iced at the gate. They returned to the gate for an inspection which revealed several damaged fan blades.
rewrite: The flight crew of an A320 experienced excessive vibration in the left engine during taxi out following de-icing and anti-icing at the gate. Upon inspection at the gate, multiple damaged fan blades were discovered, prompting a decision to return to the gate for further evaluation.

text: The pilot of a C-210 suffered total electrical failure while on an IFR flight plan in VMC. Efforts to minimize the use of electronic equipment preserved sufficient battery power to inform the Tower of the aircraft's arrival and light signals from the Tower were utilized for landing and taxi.
rewrite: During an IFR flight in VMC, a C-210 pilot experienced total electrical failure. To conserve battery power, the pilot minimized electronic equipment use and notified the Tower of arrival. The Tower used a light gun to provide landing and taxi direction via visual signals.
context: VERIFY SPECIFIC DIRECTION OF TAKEOFF (OR TURNS AFTER TAKEOFF)

text: Tower Controller chronicled a poor braking action landing event when the exact nature and location of the poor braking was confused and another aircraft was cleared to land, shortly after the runway was closed.
rewrite: Tower controllers issued a braking action advisory due to poor braking conditions on the runway. The exact nature and location of the poor braking were unclear, leading to confusion. Another aircraft was cleared to land shortly after the runway was closed.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: C172 pilot reports having his left wingtip bumped by the right wingtip of another C172 taxiing out of the runup area. The Tower is advised and eventually the other aircraft returns to the runup pad where minor damage is found to have occurred to both wingtips.
rewrite: A C172 pilot reported his left wingtip was bumped by another C172's right wingtip while taxiing out of the runup area. The tower was advised, and the involved aircraft returned to the runup pad where minor damage was found on both wingtips.

text: A Flight Instructor resigned from the flight school where she was working because, after having an electrical system malfunction at night, she felt the school's poor aircraft maintenance program put instructors and students at risk.
rewrite: A flight instructor resigned from her flight school following an electrical system malfunction during a night flight, citing concerns over the school's inadequate maintenance program, which she believed endangered both instructors and students. The incident occurred during a training session, highlighting potential safety risks associated with the school's maintenance practices. She felt the school's maintenance procedures were insufficient to ensure safe operations.

text: A B737-700 flight crew suffered TCAS TA and RAs while on vectors for landing Runway 19L at SNA.
rewrite: A B737-700 flight crew experienced a TCAS Traffic Advisory (TA) and Resolution Advisory (RA) while on radar vectors for landing Runway 19L at SNA. The aircraft was in the approach phase, following ATC instructions for a radar route. The TCAS alerts occurred as the crew was maneuvering to align with the active runway.
context: TRAFFIC ALERT AND COLLISION AVOIDANCE SYSTEM (TCAS)

text: A CRJ-700 rudder trim deflected full left with the autopilot engaged, so the QRH was completed, the rudder re-centered and the flight continued but the Captain refused the aircraft for further service after Maintenance found no faults.
rewrite: A CRJ-700 experienced full left rudder trim deflection with autopilot engaged. The QRH was completed, rudder re-centered, and the flight continued. The Captain refused the aircraft for further service after Maintenance found no faults.

text: Waco pilot and passenger report a ground loop during landing and a subsequent runway excursion with damage to the aircraft. A wind shift during landing and a significant surface drop when departing the runway edge were reported as factors in the incident.
rewrite: A Waco pilot and passenger reported a ground loop during landing, leading to a runway excursion and aircraft damage. Wind shifted during landing, and a significant surface drop was noted when departing the runway edge. The incident occurred during the landing phase, with no mention of a TOUCH-AND-GO operation.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: Tower Controller reports a possible conflict between an A320 departing Runway 27 at BOS and an SR22 flying over the downtown area.
rewrite: Tower Controller at BOS detected a potential conflict between an A320 departing Runway 27 and an SR22 flying over downtown. The controller issued a conflict alert, prompting the pilot of the departing aircraft to hold short of the runway. No further action was taken as the SR22 continued its flight path without deviation.

text: A ZDV Controller described a loss of separation when traffic inbound to D01, one via a new RNAV STAR and another on a 'Legacy' STAR conflicted.
rewrite: A ZDV controller reported a loss of separation involving two inbound aircraft on D01. One was flying a new RNAV STAR, while the other was on a 'Legacy' STAR. The conflict occurred during the en route transition segment of their respective STAR procedures.

text: A pilot reported the INT Runway 33 hold short line on Taxiway A was a greater distance from the runway than expected and the crew nearly missed seeing it.
rewrite: During LAHSO operations on Runway 33, the pilot noted the hold-short line on Taxiway A was farther from the runway than anticipated, causing the crew to nearly miss sighting it before initiating the hold-short procedure. The hold-short position marking was not easily visible, leading to a potential safety concern. The pilot promptly informed ATC of the discrepancy.

text: An overhead panel in the cabin of a CRJ-900 had been removed and replaced during installation of WiFi wiring. When it was replaced it was secured with the incorrect screws and, upon a subsequent landing, the panel fell out and struck a passenger in the head causing a painful and bloody, but not serious, injury.
rewrite: During the installation of WiFi wiring, an overhead panel in the cabin of a CRJ-900 was removed and replaced. It was secured with incorrect screws, and during a subsequent landing, the panel fell out, striking a passenger in the head and causing a painful, bloody but not serious injury.

text: Maintenance personnel discovered that the B757 forward cargo compartment ceiling panel liner was covering a smoke detector sampling tube.
rewrite: Maintenance personnel found that the B757 forward cargo compartment ceiling panel liner was obstructing a smoke detector sampling tube. The liner was covering the tube, potentially preventing proper airflow for smoke detection. This issue was identified during routine inspection on the apron.

text: A B737-700, departing ATL and inappropriately cleared to climb to 14,000 MSL, avoided a conflict with a prior departure Airbus, opposite direction at 12,000, through the alert response of the First Officer/pilot flying who stopped his climb after spotting the traffic. ATC ultimately noted the error and cleared them to descend immediately to 10,000.
rewrite: A B737-700, departing ATL, was inappropriately cleared to climb to 14,000 MSL. The pilot flying spotted an opposing Airbus at 12,000 MSL and stopped climbing, avoiding a conflict. ATC noted the error and cleared the aircraft to descend immediately to 10,000 MSL.

text: Air Carrier landing RIC was vectored direct to the airport at night and cleared for a visual approach less than five miles from the airport resulting in a go around, Controller technique was listed as a causal factor.
rewrite: An air carrier aircraft was vectored direct to the airport at night and cleared for a visual approach less than five miles from the airport, resulting in a go-around. The controller technique was listed as a causal factor. The approach was conducted without an approach gate established as required.

text: PA28 instructor pilot describes a runway excursion by his student during the second student solo in the traffic pattern.
rewrite: During the second student solo in the traffic pattern, the PA28 instructor pilot reported a runway excursion after the student attempted a straight-in approach VFR. The student failed to maintain directional control upon touchdown, resulting in the aircraft veering off the runway. The instructor initiated a go around but was unable to recover the aircraft before it came to rest off the runway.

text: A B757-200 Captain, electrically powering up a dead aircraft for preflight, inadvertently deployed the RAT believing the 'covered' RAT switch to have been the BAT switch.
rewrite: A B757-200 captain, during electrical power-up of a dead aircraft for preflight, mistakenly deployed the RAT, thinking the 'covered' RAT switch was the BAT switch. The RAT was deployed unintentionally, leading to an unexpected hydraulic system activation. The captain was unaware of the RAT deployment until noticing unusual system indications.

text: A pilot flying a PRM approach to ATL Runway 27L saw rapid glideslope fluctuations so he disconnected the autopilot and hand flew the aircraft to VMC at about 1,100 FT. On short final he saw two mowing tractors in front the ILS antenna.
rewrite: A pilot conducting a PRM approach to ATL Runway 27L experienced rapid glideslope fluctuations, prompting him to disconnect the autopilot and manually fly the aircraft to VMC at approximately 1,100 feet. On short final, he observed two mowing tractors in front of the ILS antenna.
context: LOCALIZER TYPE DIRECTIONAL AID (LDA) PRECISION RUNWAY MONITOR (PRM) APPROACH

text: Helicopter pilot, assigned as pilot not flying during an electrical transmission Tower inspection flight, reports the pilot flying operating at speeds above those prescribed by company operating specifications with external linemen attached. Reminders to the pilot flying are essentially ignored.
rewrite: During an electrical transmission tower inspection flight, the pilot not flying reported that the pilot flying operated at speeds exceeding company specifications while external linemen were attached. Despite reminders, the pilot flying did not comply with the speed restrictions.

text: CL-65 First Officer reported receiving (R) 14 DUCT message. QRH directed a diversion to nearest suitable airport.
rewrite: The CL-65 First Officer received a 14 DUCT message from radar. Following QRH procedures, the crew decided to divert to the nearest suitable airport. The pilot acknowledged the message and initiated the diversion protocol.

text: C210 pilot reported a low altitude stall and recovery while taking photographs.
rewrite: A C210 pilot experienced a low altitude stall during a flight line operation while capturing photographs. The pilot initiated a recovery and successfully regained control. The event occurred during the en route descent phase.

text: While descending IFR to 6,000 a CE-560XL flight crew responded to TCAS TA and RA alerts due to a conflict with a VFR Aero Commander allegedly at 5,500 MSL while requesting an IFR clearance.
rewrite: While descending IFR to 6,000 feet, a CE-560XL flight crew received TCAS TA and RA alerts due to a conflict with a VFR Aero Commander at 5,500 MSL. The VFR aircraft was allegedly in the same airspace, prompting the crew to respond to the conflict alert. The crew requested an IFR clearance to resolve the situation.

text: An EMB-140 Captain, while at the gate and just prior to pushback and engine start, was notified by the Agent in charge that a fuel leak had been detected emanating from the #1 engine. It was noted that the leak was one drop per second with the fuel pump on, and slowly dissipated with the fuel pump in the off position.
rewrite: An EMB-140 Captain, prior to pushback and engine start, was informed by the Agent in charge of a fuel leak from the #1 engine. The leak occurred with the fuel pump on, at a rate of one drop per second, and ceased when the pump was turned off. The leak was described as unintentional, likely due to overflow or a loose cap.

text: ZAB Controller expressed concern regarding ATC assignments made by MMZT controllers noting the same altitude was given to multiple aircraft, the reporter claiming continued systematic ATC problems along the Southern border.
rewrite: ZAB controller raised concerns about ATC assignments from MMZT controllers, noting multiple aircraft were given the same altitude. The reporter attributed ongoing systematic ATC issues along the Southern border to this practice. The controller emphasized the potential for mid-air conflicts and unsafe proximity.

text: GA5 pilot on an IFR flight had a partial communication failure, but heard clearance for an ILS approach and landed successfully. Pilot discovered that the radio problem was due to failure to engage the alternator on startup.
rewrite: GA5 pilot on an IFR flight experienced a partial communications failure but received an ILS approach clearance and landed safely. The pilot later determined the issue was due to failing to engage the alternator during startup. The radio problem was intermittent, allowing partial communication with ATC.

text: Sport Cub instructor pilot reports his student losing control due to a wind gust during a wheel landing. The instructor cannot react quickly enough and the aircraft departs the runway with the right wing tip contacting the ground.
rewrite: During a wheel landing training exercise, the student experienced a sudden wind gust, causing loss of control. The instructor pilot was unable to react in time, resulting in the aircraft departing the runway with the right wing tip touching the ground. The incident occurred during the touchdown zone phase of the landing.

text: The pilot of a glider tow aircraft was informed that while he was landing an automobile was forced to apply the brakes while traveling along the road adjacent to the grass landing strip. His standard approach was observed by the Airport Manager and it was determined to be safe.
rewrite: The pilot of a glider tow aircraft was advised that an automobile on the adjacent road had to brake suddenly. The pilot executed a standard approach to the grass landing strip, which was observed by the Airport Manager and deemed safe. No landing zone designation was provided as the strip is a military landing zone.

text: ZDC Controller described a near airspace infraction when a ZNY Controller had incorrectly advised a pilot of the status of R4001.
rewrite: The ZDC controller reported a near airspace infraction involving a ZNY controller who incorrectly advised a pilot regarding the status of R4001. The ZNY controller provided inaccurate information, leading to potential conflict. PREARRANGED COORDINATION PROCEDURES were not followed, resulting in a safety concern.

text: A DA20 instructor pilot and his student in the traffic pattern experienced an NMAC with a Piper Seneca that had taken off after them but passed overhead 100 FT while on downwind.
rewrite: A DA20 instructor and student were in the traffic pattern when an NMAC occurred with a Piper Seneca that had departed after them. The Seneca passed overhead at 100 FT while the DA20 was on downwind. The incident involved a potential conflict in the traffic pattern during a training session.

text: ZBW Controller described an unsafe condition when traffic being transferred to his/her frequency contained inaccurate data block information activating a false 'Conflict Alert'.
rewrite: ZBW controller reported an unsafe condition when traffic transferred to his frequency had an unassociated data block, triggering a false conflict alert. The inaccurate information led to a conflict alert activation, prompting immediate controller action to resolve the situation. The controller issued a safety alert due to the potential unsafe proximity caused by the erroneous data.

text: The Captain of an A321 failed to note when his First Officer, new to the airline, loaded the route in the FMS incorrectly. A track deviation ensued.
rewrite: The Captain of an A321 failed to notice when the First Officer, new to the airline, input an incorrect route into the FMS. This led to a track deviation exceeding 10 NM from the cleared route, constituting a gross navigation error. The deviation occurred during the en-route phase of the flight.

text: An Air Carrier crew took evasive action responding to a TCAS RA at FL340 eastbound near OMEKA Intersection after Gander erroneously issued a climb clearance to a westbound aircraft.
rewrite: An Air Carrier crew executed evasive action in response to a TCAS RA at FL340 while eastbound near OMEKA Intersection. The Gander controller mistakenly issued a climb clearance to a westbound aircraft, leading to the conflict. The clearance limit was not properly coordinated, resulting in the unexpected vertical separation issue.

text: B737-700 Captain reported a wake vortex encounter on descent into BNA that provided enough distraction they missed a crossing restriction.
rewrite: During descent into BNA, the B737-700 Captain reported a wake vortex encounter that caused significant distraction, leading to a missed crossing restriction at a specified fix. The pilot was supposed to cross the fix at or above a designated altitude, but the distraction resulted in non-compliance. The encounter occurred during the Runway Profile Descent phase of the approach.

text: Air Carrier flight crew and the Dispatcher involved report a go-around at ABQ due to severe turbulence on approach to Runway 26. The crew continues on a westerly heading to avoid the weather and eventually requests direct to their alternate, but does not proceed as cleared continuing to discuss options. ATC questions the crew, but by this time flights are getting in and the crew elects to land at ABQ and does so safely.
rewrite: Air Carrier flight crew and Dispatcher reported a go-around at ABQ due to severe turbulence on approach to Runway 26. The crew continued west to avoid weather, requested direct to alternate, but did not proceed as cleared. ATC questioned the crew, but flights were inbound, so they elected to land at ABQ safely.

text: B737 flight crew enroute to a foreign destination, decided to return to their departure airport due to an unruly aggressive passenger who had to be restrained and handcuffed.
rewrite: A B737 crew en route to a foreign destination encountered an unruly, aggressive passenger who required restraint and handcuffing. The crew decided to return to the departure airport to manage the situation. The flight plan was altered from a ROUND to a direct return, with no stopover.

text: An international relief pilot for an air carrier expressed misgivings about the implementation of a tablet type EFB by his airline, citing training, spares, battery issues and lack of 24/7 support.
rewrite: An international relief pilot for an air carrier voiced concerns regarding the implementation of a tablet-based EFB, citing inadequate training, spares, battery life, and the absence of 24/7 technical support. The pilot highlighted operational challenges during flight phases, emphasizing the need for reliable equipment and continuous assistance. The airline's approach to EFB integration was questioned for its readiness and support infrastructure.

text: A B757 First Officer's Flight Directer OFF flap appeared at about the same time as an electrical odor was detected in both the flight station and cabin so the flight diverted to a nearby airport for a normal landing.
rewrite: A B757 First Officer reported that the Flight Director's OFF flap indication appeared simultaneously with an electrical odor detected in both the flight deck and cabin. The crew decided to divert to a nearby airport for a normal landing due to the unusual conditions.

text: MD11 flight crew experiences the loss of the number three hydraulic system while configuring for landing. A go-around is initiated, the QRH is consulted and the gear is manually extended.
rewrite: MD11 flight crew experienced loss of hydraulic system three while configuring for landing. They initiated a go-around and consulted the QRH. The gear was manually extended to complete the maneuver.

text: C172 pilot experienced a runway incursion at LGB. Reporter stated confusing signage was a contributing factor.
rewrite: A C172 pilot reported a runway incursion at LGB, attributing the incident to confusing signage. The pilot indicated the area was a HOT SPOT, and the situation was exacerbated by unclear markings. The pilot did not report any braking action or traffic advisories during the event.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: A321 Captain describes an encounter with unexpected moderate to severe turbulence at FL330 causing the aircraft to climb 900 FT before returning to assigned altitude.
rewrite: A321 Captain reported encountering unexpected moderate to severe turbulence at FL330, resulting in an uncommanded climb of 900 FT. The aircraft stabilized and returned to the assigned altitude. The turbulence was not forecasted and occurred during cruise.

text: Low oil pressure indications and a failing pressurization system convinced a Convair 580 flight crew to divert to a nearby airport. Although the right engine was shut down as a precautionary measure, no emergency was declared.
rewrite: A Convair 580 crew diverted to a nearby airport due to low oil pressure indications and a failing pressurization system. The right engine was shut down as a precaution, but no emergency was declared. The crew managed the situation without activating the emergency autoland system.

text: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) realizes he improperly ordered an inboard Slat Disconnect Sensor for a CRJ-900 aircraft through the parts computer ordering system of their merged Air Carrier's inventory program, instead of using their own parts ordering system. He noticed the incorrect serviceable tag after returning from a field trip.
rewrite: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) identified an error in parts ordering, having selected an inboard Slat Disconnect Sensor for a CRJ-900 via the merged Air Carrier's inventory program instead of the AMT's own parts ordering system. The mistake was discovered after the AMT returned from a field trip, noticing the incorrect serviceable tag on the part.

text: PA28 pilot on an IFR flight plan reports being distracted by a radio problem and allowing his heading to drift off course by 45-50 degrees before correcting.
rewrite: A PA28 pilot on an IFR flight plan reported being distracted by a radio problem, leading to a heading drift of 45-50 degrees from the assigned course.
