text: ZAB Controller describes a shift where weather is causing aircraft to deviate and that the controllers are trying to recall restricted airspace to allow flights better deviations.
rewrite: ZAB Controller reported a shift where weather caused aircraft to deviate from their cleared routes. Controllers attempted to recall restricted airspace to facilitate better deviations. Several flights experienced gross navigation errors due to the challenging weather conditions.

text: After departure a B737-900ER crew received and entered a revised zero fuel weight of 113.8 in the FMS. At FL390 the weight and balance was reexamined because of sluggish performance and the correct weight of 133.8 entered which required a descent to FL370.
rewrite: After departure, the B737-900ER crew received and entered a revised zero fuel weight of 113.8 in the FMS. At FL390, the weight and balance was reexamined due to sluggish performance, and the correct weight of 133.8 was entered, requiring a descent to FL370.

text: B737 Flight Attendant is informed by an FAA Inspector that a FAOM revision dated in the future must be installed during the flight, in order to be compliant with FAR's. The Inspector also does not comply with the reporters request to remain clear of the forward galley while the Captain is out of the cockpit and sits on a jumpseat.
rewrite: An FAA Inspector informed a B737 Flight Attendant that a future-dated FAOM revision must be installed during the flight to comply with FARs. The Inspector refused the reporter's request to stay clear of the forward galley while the Captain was out of the cockpit and seated on the jumpseat.

text: When a homeowner near the airport found an aircraft shimmy dampener from a PA-28 had fallen through the roof of his home he was able to track down the aircraft via the part type and investigation of such equipped aircraft at the airport. The reports were submitted by the pilot undergoing a BFR and his check airman who had flown the offending aircraft during the time period in question.
rewrite: A homeowner near the airport discovered a PA-28 aircraft shimmy dampener that had fallen through his roof. He identified the aircraft by the part type and traced it to a specific aircraft at the airport. The incident was reported by the pilot completing a BFR and his check airman, who had flown the aircraft during the relevant time period.

text: An AA5 pilot suffered engine failure after switching tanks and landed in a plowed field, suffering a collapse of the nose gear. Water in the left fuel tank was the apparent cause.
rewrite: An AA5 pilot experienced a flameout after switching fuel tanks, leading to an engine failure. The aircraft was forced to land in a plowed field, resulting in a collapsed nose gear. Water in the left fuel tank was identified as the probable cause.

text: The number one engine oil quantity decreased to zero followed by an oil pressure drop, so the engine was shutdown, an emergency declared and the flight diverted to a nearby airport for an uneventful emergency landing. A gear box oil line had sheared.
rewrite: The number one engine oil quantity dropped to zero, causing an oil pressure loss and subsequent engine shutdown. An emergency was declared, and the flight diverted to a nearby airport for an emergency landing. A gear box oil line had sheared during the incident.

text: A MD-80 First Officer discovered both the Main and Alternate trim inoperative upon leveling at cruise. The QRH was completed but all systems appeared normal, then prior to descent both trim systems became operational. An uneventful landing ensued.
rewrite: A MD-80 First Officer noted both main and alternate trim systems inoperative upon leveling off at cruise altitude. The QRH was completed, and all systems appeared normal. Prior to descent, both trim systems became operational, resulting in an uneventful landing.

text: B737-300 First Officer reports getting very slow after using gear and flaps to get down, when the aircraft banks hard to capture the localizer and pitches up to capture altitude with the engines at idle and no autothrust.
rewrite: A B737-300 First Officer reports a significant loss of airspeed after deploying gear and flaps for descent. The aircraft then banks abruptly to capture the localizer and pitches up to attain the assigned altitude with engines at idle and autothrust disengaged. The slow speed persists despite these actions.

text: A CRJ-700 crew taxiing to SFO Runway 1R missed the turn onto the new Taxiway A1 from Alpha because their Airport Diagram had not been updated but, unbeknown to them, was available at their domicile for SFO trips.
rewrite: A CRJ-700 crew taxiing to SFO Runway 1R missed the turn onto the new Taxiway A1 from Alpha due to an outdated Airport Diagram at their domicile. The updated diagram was available at their base but not carried onboard. This led to a deviation from the taxi pattern, requiring ATC intervention to reposition the aircraft.

text: C414 pilot reports rejecting a takeoff due to lack of directional control. The rudder gust lock had not been removed during preflight.
rewrite: C414 pilot rejected takeoff due to lack of directional control. Rudder gust lock was not removed during preflight. The issue was identified during the preflight inspection before initiating the takeoff roll.
context: VERIFY SPECIFIC DIRECTION OF TAKEOFF (OR TURNS AFTER TAKEOFF)

text: A B737-800 returned to the gate with an Antiskid INOP indication and both systems were MEL'ED because the faulty system was not identified. In the rush to release the aircraft, the flight station downgrade was not accomplished.
rewrite: A B737-800 returned to the gate with an Antiskid INOP indication. Both systems were MEL'ed as the faulty system could not be identified. The flight station downgrade was not completed due to the rush to release the aircraft.

text: A B737-800 crew became distracted during pushback and engine start by ATC changing the runway and departure. While recalculating performance data the First Officer failed to lower flaps which the crew discovered when the Taxi Checklist was reviewed during taxi.
rewrite: ATC changed the runway and departure during pushback and engine start, causing distraction for the B737-800 crew. While recalculating performance data, the First Officer failed to lower the flaps. The error was discovered when the Taxi Checklist was reviewed during taxi.

text: Citabria pilot experiences the loss of the cabin door in flight over an unpopulated area. Pilot diverts to a suitable airport.
rewrite: A Citabria pilot experienced a loss of the cabin door during flight over an unpopulated area. The pilot initiated a diversion to a suitable airport to ensure safety. The incident occurred during cruise phase with no immediate control issues reported.

text: EMB145 flight crew detects smoke in the cockpit and the Flight Attendant detects it in the cabin. The flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport where maintenance determines that the left pack is likely the culprit and is MEL'd. The passengers are reboarded and the flight departs. The odor is again detected causing another diversion.
rewrite: An EMB145 flight crew detected smoke in the cockpit while the flight attendant identified the odor in the cabin. The flight diverted to the nearest suitable airport, where maintenance determined the left pack was the likely source and it was MEL'd. Passengers were reboarded, but the odor reappeared, prompting another diversion.

text: BE33 instructor and two students report a NMAC with a small low wing aircraft about 6 NM south of CHD at 2,500 FT. The other aircraft was detected too late to take evasive action and passed within 200 FT. The other aircraft did not have an operating transponder.
rewrite: BE33 instructor and two students encountered a near mid-air collision (NMAC) with a small low-wing aircraft approximately 6 NM south of CHD at 2,500 feet. The other aircraft was detected too late to take evasive action, passing within 200 feet. The involved aircraft did not have an operating transponder.

text: Flight instructor reports being unable to locate Taxiway C5 while southbound on Taxiway C due to no sign at the intersection. Airport construction is underway.
rewrite: Flight instructor was southbound on Taxiway C and unable to locate Taxiway C5 at the intersection due to the absence of a sign. Airport construction was ongoing, which may have obscured or removed existing signage. The hold line and markings were not visible, complicating navigation.

text: During approach, B737-800 flight crew experiences autopilot and flight director anomalies and the autopilot cannot be reconnected. The Captain elected to go-around. On the second approach autopilots and approach mode can still not be selected but the First Officer had a functioning flight director and flies the approach to landing.
rewrite: During the final approach, the B737-800 flight crew encountered autopilot and flight director anomalies, preventing autopilot reengagement. The Captain initiated a missed approach. On the second attempt, autopilot and approach mode remained unavailable, but the First Officer utilized the functioning flight director to manually complete the approach and land.

text: MYF Tower controller describes a NMAC caused by a pilot not familiar with the local procedures while airborne.
rewrite: The MYF Tower controller reported a near mid-air collision (NMAC) involving an aircraft unfamiliar with local procedures. The pilot was airborne and failed to comply with prearranged coordination procedures, leading to an unsafe situation. The controller had to intervene to prevent a potential conflict in the local traffic area.

text: A320 Captain reports being confused by a Marshall's taxi directions, resulting in the aircraft being towed into the gate. The Captain believes that the Marshall has not been properly trained to perform the new SOP.
rewrite: A320 Captain reported confusion with Marshall's taxi instructions, leading to the aircraft being towed to the gate. The Captain suspected the Marshall lacked proper training for the new SOP. The incident occurred during the taxi phase.

text: B737 Captain reports arriving at the aircraft 29 minutes prior to departure due to transportation issues to find the aircraft half boarded and the lead Flight Attendant requesting the power be turned on. The battery switch was off, emergency exit lights were not armed and they could not make PA's with the power off.
rewrite: A B737 captain arrived 29 minutes early due to transportation delays to find the aircraft partially boarded. The lead flight attendant requested power be turned on as the battery switch was off, emergency exit lights were not armed, and passenger announcements could not be made without power.
context: VERIFY SPECIFIC DIRECTION OF TAKEOFF (OR TURNS AFTER TAKEOFF)

text: ZDV Controller reports of discovering an aircraft that he was working, was below the MIA.
rewrite: The ZDV controller detected an aircraft under his responsibility descending below the Minimum IFR Altitude (MIA) while en route, triggering an En Route Minimum Safe Altitude Warning (E: MSAW). The controller issued a prompt alert and initiated procedures to ensure the aircraft regained compliance with the established MIA. The situation required immediate attention to maintain safe separation and adherence to airspace regulations.
context: EN ROUTE MINIMUM SAFE ALTITUDE WARNING (E

text: A commercial rated pilot and his flight instructor in a PA-34 Piper Seneca experienced a nose landing gear collapse after landing for unknown reasons.
rewrite: A commercial-rated pilot and his flight instructor in a PA-34 Piper Seneca experienced a nose landing gear collapse following a landing, with the cause of the failure unknown. The incident occurred during a flight test, and the aircraft was cleared for the option to perform a full stop landing. No prior mechanical issues were reported.
context: DELAY INDEFINITE (REASON IF KNOWN) EXPECT FURTHER CLEARANCE (TIME)

text: CE-560XL flight crew reported ACM Overheat light illuminated on climb out, accompanied by smoke and odor. Flight declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
rewrite: CE-560XL flight crew reported ACM Overheat light illuminated during climb out, accompanied by smoke and odor. The flight declared an emergency and initiated a return to the departure airport. The crew executed a visual climb over the airport (VCOA) to the published climb-to altitude before proceeding with the return.

text: Helicopter pilot reported an NMAC with a Cessna at PRC airport when he misunderstood his taxi clearance.
rewrite: Helicopter pilot reported an NMAC with a Cessna at PRC airport during taxi. The pilot misunderstood his taxi clearance, leading to an unsafe proximity situation. The helicopter was conducting a hover taxi, and the Cessna was on the surface.

text: A Mcdonnell Douglas widebody flight crew experienced a stick shaker and SLAS DISAG alert as the aircraft was slowed through 150 KTS during approach. A go-around is initiated and a second approach with higher Vspeeds results in the same alerts and another go-around. The next approach is accomplished with the slats retracted to a successful landing.
rewrite: During the final approach segment, a McDonnell Douglas widebody crew encountered a stick shaker and SLAS DISAG alert while decelerating to 150 KTS. After initiating a go-around and attempting a second approach with increased V-speeds, the same alerts occurred, prompting another go-around. The third approach was conducted with slats retracted, resulting in a successful landing.

text: B737-300 flight crew reported noticing strong electrical fumes and electrical system anomalies during taxi. They returned to the gate for maintenance.
rewrite: During taxi, the B737-300 flight crew detected strong electrical fumes and electrical system anomalies. The pilot-in-command requested a tarmac delay to return to the gate for maintenance. The aircraft was classified as a tarmac delay aircraft under the Three-hour Tarmac Rule.

text: MEM Tower Local Control describes a situation where they had to take an aircraft out for resequence due to its speed on final.
rewrite: MEM Tower Local Control reported a need to resequence an aircraft on final approach due to its excessive speed, which posed a potential conflict with the traffic pattern. The controller issued instructions to delay the landing to maintain proper spacing and sequencing within the local traffic area. The situation involved a nonapproach control tower managing aircraft operations in the airport advisory area.

text: The First Officer of a Gulfstream G200 related repeated attempts to get the Captain's attention to their divergent track and altitude while attempting to fly the ILS Runway 6 to TEB during turbulent but VMC. Following a low altitude alert from the Tower they began a go-around but then picked up the airport and landed safely. The reporter attributed the Captain's disorientation to automation dependency.
rewrite: The First Officer of a Gulfstream G200 repeatedly called out divergent track and altitude while flying the ILS Runway 6 approach to TEB during turbulence in VMC. After a low altitude alert from Tower, they initiated a go-around, then regained the airport and landed safely. The report suggests the Captain's disorientation was due to automation dependency.
context: EN ROUTE MINIMUM SAFE ALTITUDE WARNING (E

text: CRQ Controllers report of an aircraft that gets a flat tire while exiting the runway but stops within the safety area of the runway. Operations continue even though the aircraft is in the safety area.
rewrite: CRQ controllers reported an aircraft experiencing a flat tire while exiting the runway but stopping within the safety area. The aircraft remained in the safety area without exiting or crossing the runway. Operations continued as the aircraft was clear of the runway per controller procedures.

text: TRACON Controller describes hearing an ELT on the previous shift and remembers hearing being reported to the FLM on duty. The next shift he hears about another ELT and wonders if it was the same aircraft from the night before. The Controller wonders if the FLM took actions to locate the ELT.
rewrite: The TRACON controller recalls hearing an ELT activation during the previous shift and notes it was reported to the FLM on duty. On the next shift, he hears of another ELT and questions if it pertains to the same aircraft. He is unsure if the FLM initiated any actions to locate the ELT.

text: EMB-145LR Captain reported deviating from cleared track on departure when the flying First Officer called for LNAV prematurely.
rewrite: EMB-145LR Captain deviated from cleared track on departure after First Officer called for LNAV prematurely. The deviation resulted in a gross navigation error, with the aircraft flying a different flight path than cleared. The pilot reported the deviation to ATC, indicating a loss of lateral separation.

text: ZID Controller describes a situation where an aircraft is outside of a Restricted Area maneuvering while IFR.
rewrite: ZID Controller reported an aircraft operating under IFR outside a restricted area, maneuvering without adherence to the prescribed overhead maneuver procedures. The controller noted the aircraft's deviation from the established pattern and issued instructions to re-enter the VFR traffic pattern. The situation required immediate attention due to potential conflict with other traffic.

text: ZFW Controller thinks he issued a lower altitude to an aircraft and put that altitude in the data block. Controller ships aircraft to next sector and observes aircraft climbing above altitude that he thought he was assigned.
rewrite: The ZFW controller believed he issued a lower altitude to an aircraft and included it in the data block. He transferred the aircraft to the next sector, then noticed the aircraft climbing above the altitude he thought was assigned. The aircraft's climb indicated a discrepancy between the controller's assigned altitude and the actual altitude in the data block.

text: CARJ Captain discovers that the liquid used to service the aft lavitory is contaminated with gasoline that filled the aircraft with overwhelming fumes and vapors. It is suggested but never verified that the lav service company uses gasoline to prevent the liquid from freezing. The flight is canceled.
rewrite: CARJ Captain reports contamination of aft lavatory service liquid with gasoline, resulting in overwhelming fumes and vapors filling the aircraft. The liquid, possibly used to prevent freezing, was supplied by the lav service company. The flight was subsequently canceled.

text: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports he had attached an electrical lead on a CRJ-700 aircraft to an incorrect position during installation of Junction Box (JB-5) in the Aft Electrical Equipment Bay. The cross-connection caused a spark and burn mark on the part he installed. Limited Shift turnover information and inadequate visual reference diagrams were contributors.
rewrite: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) incorrectly attached an electrical lead to the Junction Box (JB-5) in the Aft Electrical Equipment Bay of a CRJ-700, resulting in a spark and burn mark. The error was attributed to limited shift turnover information and inadequate visual reference diagrams. The cross-connection occurred during JB-5 installation.

text: A station agent unfamiliar with, and apparently, untrained on weight and balance computations for the B737-800, provided passenger numbers and distribution which met the computation demands but did not reflect the actual location of the passengers on board. When computed with their actual location the resulting trim setting was rejected as out of limits. Relocating the passengers produced a valid and operationally acceptable center of gravity and the flight departed.
rewrite: A station agent, untrained in weight and balance calculations for the B737-800, provided passenger numbers and distribution that met computational requirements but did not reflect actual passenger locations. When using actual positions, the center of gravity exceeded limits. Relocating passengers resulted in an acceptable center of gravity, allowing the flight to depart.

text: B737 FO reported getting low on a visual approach to PDX when the pilot flying lost autopilot mode awareness.
rewrite: During a visual approach to PDX, the B737 flight operations officer reported low on fuel. The pilot flying lost autopilot mode awareness, leading to potential disengagement of the autopilot during the visual segment of the approach. The crew was required to manually manage the approach without autopilot assistance.
context: PUBLISHED INSTRUMENT APPROACH PROCEDURE VISUAL SEGMENT

text: A320 flight crew experiences a terrain warning at 5100 feet south of SJC in night IMC, while being vectored by NCT. Evasive action is taken by the crew, climbing to 6000 feet although NCT states that 5100 feet is the correct MVA for that area. The Captain believes the turbulence may have been a factor in the false terrain warning.
rewrite: An A320 flight crew received a terrain warning at 5100 feet south of SJC during night IMC while being vectored by NCT. The crew initiated evasive action, climbing to 6000 feet despite NCT confirming 5100 feet as the correct MVA for the area. The Captain suspects turbulence may have contributed to the false terrain warning.

text: OAK Tower controller reports of two aircraft that depart OKA and do not follow the SID restrictions and climb above crossing altitudes.
rewrite: OAK Tower reported two aircraft departing OKA that failed to comply with SID altitude restrictions. Both climbed above the assigned crossing altitudes at specified fixes. The controllers noted the violations but did not issue corrective actions.

text: Dispatcher reports an aircraft departing with 1,300 pounds of cargo in the aft pit that was to be removed to comply with aircraft C.G. limits. Miscommunication between the parties involved allowed the aircraft to depart without the cargo being removed.
rewrite: Dispatcher reported an aircraft departing with 1,300 pounds of cargo in the aft pit, intended for removal to comply with aircraft CG limits. Miscommunication between dispatcher and crew allowed the cargo to remain onboard, resulting in an overweight condition at departure. The cargo was not removed as planned.

text: B747 flight crew experiences a loud bang from the nose gear area when the landing gear is selected up. EICAS landing gear disagree and gear door disagree messages were displayed. When the gear is selected down in compliance with QRH procedures another loud bang is heard and vibration is noted on the number two engine. The crew elects to discontinue QRH procedures and return to the departure airport.
rewrite: A B747 flight crew heard a loud bang from the nose gear area upon selecting up the landing gear, with EICAS displaying landing gear disagree and gear door disagree messages. When attempting to lower the gear per QRH procedures, another bang and vibration on the number two engine occurred. The crew terminated QRH procedures and decided to return to the departure airport.

text: On approach to HOU at about 700 feet, flight crew was struck by a green laser light flash. They were able to continue the approach and landed.
rewrite: On approach to HOU at approximately 700 feet, the flight crew encountered a green laser light flash. The crew was able to continue the approach and complete the landing without further incident. No mention of airport rotating beacon or other lighting systems was noted in the report.

text: A B737 flight crew went around after a GPWS alert sounded while they were circling to land at SFO on RWY 01L. On the next approach they shortened the final segment from five miles to three miles and were able to fly the approach without the GPWS sounding.
rewrite: A B737 flight crew initiated a go-around after a GPWS alert during a circling approach to SFO on RWY 01L. On the subsequent approach, they shortened the final approach segment from five miles to three miles, allowing them to complete the approach without triggering the GPWS.

text: CRJ-900 Captain reported that after a wake vortex encounter in a holding pattern, the left engine ITT increased abnormally, perhaps due to a compressor stall.
rewrite: During a holding pattern, a CRJ-900 Captain experienced a wake vortex encounter, leading to an abnormal increase in the left engine ITT, which may have been caused by a compressor stall. The pilot noted the unusual temperature rise without any immediate loss of thrust or other anomalies. The event occurred during the airborne delay phase while maintaining the minimum holding altitude.

text: HNL Controller reports of an operational error due to two aircraft landing at the same time on crossing runways. No go-around instructions were issued to any aircraft.
rewrite: HNL controller observed an operational error during landing phase when two aircraft landed on crossing runways simultaneously. No go-around instructions were issued to either aircraft. The situation involved LAND AND HOLD SHORT OPERATIONS with both aircraft holding short of intersecting taxiways.

text: A319 flight crew departing SFO on the SSTIK1 reports receiving several vectors and ultimately direct NTELL, prior to reaching PORTE. The crew levels at 10,000 feet since they have not passed PORTE, which is not what ATC was expecting.
rewrite: An A319 flight crew departing SFO on the SSTIK1 departure procedure received multiple vectors and was ultimately directed to NTELL before reaching PORTE. The crew leveled off at 10,000 feet as they had not yet passed PORTE, which was not the expected ATC clearance.

text: Flight crew of a CRJ-200 repositioning flight for maintenance were planned for FL320, gear down flight at 250 KIAS. Enroute aircraft is only able to climb to FL240 max altitude thus dipping into their fuel reserves and forcing a diversion. Flight refuels and continues on to intended destination.
rewrite: Flight crew operating a CRJ-200 on a repositioning flight for maintenance filed for FL320 with gear down at 250 KIAS. The enroute aircraft was unable to climb above FL240, resulting in fuel reserve depletion and a diversion. The flight refueled and continued to the intended destination.

text: HCF Controller describes a situation where an aircraft departs an airport under their control but does not follow the standard departure. Aircraft turns incorrectly and is in an area with a low MVA. Controller issues a vector towards a lower MVA and flight resumes safely.
rewrite: An aircraft departed under radar vectors but deviated from the standard departure procedure, turning into a low MVA area. The controller issued a vector toward a lower MVA, allowing the flight to resume safely. The pilot then resumed own navigation.

text: An air carrier on the SFO 28R localizer took evasive action and executed a go around after another air carrier on the 28L localizer drifted 400 feet over them with no ATC intervention.
rewrite: An air carrier operating on the SFO 28R localizer initiated a go-around after another air carrier on the 28L localizer drifted 400 feet over their flight path without ATC intervention during the night. The incident occurred in the local traffic area, with both aircraft in the traffic pattern. No ATC action was taken to resolve the conflict.

text: SCT Controller describes a loss of separation between a HHR arrival and a LGB departure.
rewrite: SCT controller reported a loss of separation between a HHR arrival and a LGB departure during the arrival/departure window. The automated terminal proximity alert triggered a yellow cone at 45 seconds and a red cone at 24 seconds prior to predicted loss of separation. The controller initiated prearranged coordination procedures to manage the conflict.

text: A single engine aircraft experienced engine failure two times. The pilot was unable to restart after the second loss and landed in a polo field. He stated that there was no damage to the aircraft.
rewrite: A single-engine aircraft experienced a flameout, resulting in engine failure. The pilot attempted to restart but was unsuccessful, leading to a second engine shutdown. Unable to regain power, the pilot executed an emergency landing in a polo field, reporting no damage to the aircraft.

text: An EMB145 flight crew rejected their takeoff at ~100KIAS upon receipt of an EICAS baggage door open message. The reporter cited snow covered runways, braking action fair reports, reduced visibility and being well above 80KIAS as factors making the go/no go decision difficult.
rewrite: An EMB145 crew rejected takeoff at approximately 100 KIAS after receiving an EICAS baggage door open message. The flight was operating on snow-covered runways with fair braking action, reduced visibility, and a high speed above 80 KIAS, complicating the go/no-go decision. The crew opted to abort due to the reported condition and potential safety risk.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: A pilot reports about cracks that develop in a bracket attached to the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) strut that are not deferrable on Hawker HS-125-800 XP aircraft, causing delays and cancellations. Bracket supports a squat switch that controls the wing landing lights and taxi lights.
rewrite: A pilot reports cracks developing in a bracket attached to the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) strut on a Hawker HS-125-800 XP aircraft, which is not deferrable. The bracket supports a squat switch that controls the wing landing lights and taxi lights. The issue caused delays and cancellations.

text: B737-700 FO reported the Captain was rushing the flight to make his commute home, making the FO very uncomfortable and leading to a possible zero flap takeoff.
rewrite: A B737-700 first officer reported the captain was rushing the flight to make his commute, causing discomfort and raising concerns about a possible zero flap takeoff. The situation occurred during the departure phase, with the FO noting the captain's urgency and potential compromise of standard operating procedures.

text: B737 Captain is in formed during approach by the Flight Attendants that both lavatory smoke alarms are going off but no smoke was seen. The approach is continued and just before landing the Equipment exhaust cooling light and the Auto Fail light came on. the aircraft continues to the gate with ARFF following but no smoke is ever seen.
rewrite: During the approach, the B737 captain was informed by flight attendants that both lavatory smoke alarms activated, though no smoke was visible. The approach was continued, and just before landing, the Equipment Exhaust Cooling Light and Auto Fail light illuminated. The aircraft proceeded to the gate with ARFF in attendance, but no smoke was observed.

text: B737-700 Captain reported difficulty finding their assigned standard taxi route after landing at ATL, citing unintuitive indexing practices used in their EFB as contributing.
rewrite: A B737-700 captain reported difficulty locating the assigned standard taxi route at Atlanta (ATL) following landing, attributing the challenge to unintuitive indexing within their EFB. The pilot indicated confusion with the display layout, which hindered efficient taxi navigation. Progressive taxi instructions were requested to assist in maneuvering to the assigned stand.

text: After descending to FL240 due to turbulence the flight crew of an A320 was cleared to descend via the IVANE RNAV STAR to CLT. Although they had set FL240 as a firm crossing on their preplanned programming of the arrival they failed to realize that so doing satisfied the crossing restriction at MAYOS (Between FL260 & FL240) and, thus, the restriction was removed from consideration by the FMGC. When they selected a VNAV/Managed Descent the FMGC factored the next crossing at KIYEN (At or above FL220) and began a descent...thus triggering the deviation. The Primary reporter cited reliance on automation as a contributing factor.
rewrite: After descending to FL240 due to turbulence, the A320 flight crew was cleared to descend via the IVANE RNAV STAR to CLT. They had set FL240 as a firm crossing in their preplanned arrival, but this satisfied the crossing restriction at MAYOS (between FL260 and FL240), removing it from consideration by the FMGC. When they selected VNAV/Managed Descent, the FMGC factored the next crossing at KIYEN (at or above FL220) and initiated a descent, causing a

text: An A319 flight crew, level at FL220 near MSTRD and cleared via the IVANE RNAV STAR to CLT, was cleared to 'descend via' the arrival and the flight crew selected managed descent after confirming that each had reviewed the procedure, its restrictions and had determined and set the 'bottom altitude' for the procedure as 6,000 MSL. The aircraft then began a descent to cross ROYOS between FL230 and FL190 as charted, but failed to meet the requirement to cross the active waypoint, KIYEN, at or above FL220 as restricted.
rewrite: An A319 flight crew, level at FL220 near MSTRD, was cleared via the IVANE RNAV STAR to CLT and instructed to descend via the arrival. After confirming procedure review and setting a bottom altitude of 6,000 MSL, the crew initiated a descent to cross ROYOS between FL230 and FL190. However, they failed to cross KIYEN at or above FL220 as required.

text: A pilot reported that because MCX and OXI are in close proximity and share a common CTAF frequency, sometimes an aircraft's location is confused. Reporter stated some pilots do not clearly speak the respective airport names adding to the confusion.
rewrite: A pilot reported confusion due to MCX and OXI being in close proximity and sharing a common CTAF frequency. Some pilots fail to clearly state the respective airport names, leading to misidentification. This ambiguity can result in incorrect location reporting and potential safety risks.
context: DESIGNATED COMMON TRAFFIC ADVISORY FREQUENCY (CTAF) AREA

text: A Captain reports their A320 MEL and Flight Manuals are not specific enough to determine if an MEL 29-30-03F of an ECAM Hydraulics Page Indications, System Pressure is appropriate for the system failure being addressed. First Officer (FO) had noticed on the ECAM HYD Page that a line extending up from the blue pump was green instead of amber as it should be with no Blue System pressure.
rewrite: The Captain reported that the A320 MEL and Flight Manuals lacked clarity on whether the ECAM Hydraulics Page Indication for MEL 29-30-03F was applicable to the current system failure. The First Officer observed a green line extending from the blue pump on the ECAM HYD page, which should have been amber when no Blue System pressure was present.

text: A CLT (Charlotte) Controller describes situation where Ramp Tower controllers don't have aircraft move to clear the active runway because the alley is blocked.
rewrite: A CLT Ramp Tower controller reported that aircraft were not moving to clear the active runway because the alley was blocked, preventing them from reaching the holding position. The controller noted that the nonapproach control tower was unable to sequence aircraft effectively due to the obstruction. This led to a potential conflict with the active runway usage.

text: Single pilot C441 pilot departing VGT believes he may have climbed above 5,000 feet at RUZCO while on the NOTWN3 SID. Reporter believes ATC gave him initial altitude of 7000 feet which he believes contributed to the altitude bust. Reporter also cites receiving the SID after engine start leaving very little time to brief new routing.
rewrite: Single pilot C441 departed VGT and climbed above 5,000 feet at RUZCO during NOTWN3 SID. Pilot believes ATC assigned initial altitude of 7,000 feet, contributing to the altitude bust. He also states receiving the SID after engine start, leaving insufficient time for briefing.

text: ORD Tower controllers report of a runway incursion they observed.
rewrite: ORD Tower controllers observed a runway incursion involving a departing aircraft and a vehicle on the active runway. The incident occurred during departure roll, with the vehicle entering the runway without clearance. Controllers initiated emergency procedures and alerted the appropriate authorities.

text: ZOA controller reports of issues with the BUTTES Sector at NCT not accepting hand offs. NCT controllers admit [according to reporter] not setting up their scopes to see far enough into ZOA's R-44 airspace.
rewrite: ZOA controller reports issues with the BUTTES Sector at NCT not accepting handoffs. NCT controllers admit not setting up their scopes to see far enough into ZOA's R-44 airspace, affecting surveillance approach procedures and common point management. This led to communication challenges and potential separation issues during controlled airspace operations.

text: An EMB-145 air crew were given instructions to taxi to the gate with no restrictions. While taxiing, another aircraft being taxied by maintenance personnel cut them off at a high rate of speed. Ground control would not answer calls. The Captain called the Tower on the telephone and was informed that they were training a controller that evening.
rewrite: An EMB-145 crew was instructed to taxi to the gate with no restrictions. While taxiing, maintenance personnel operating another aircraft cut them off at a high speed. The crew attempted to contact Ground Control but received no response. The Captain then called Tower and was informed they were training a controller that evening.

text: C208B Captain reported icing in flight that made it impossible to maintain minimum vectoring altitude in an area of high terrain. They descended to warmer air and landed safely at departure airport.
rewrite: The C208B captain reported icing that prevented maintaining the minimum vectoring altitude in a high terrain area. The crew descended to warmer air and landed safely at the departure airport. Icing compromised the ability to maintain the required altitude due to terrain constraints.

text: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports finding three Crew Oxygen bottles with damaged (bent) pressure gauges during a Receiving Inspection procedure prior to putting the bottles in service. Concerns also raised as to where the damage had been occurring and whether other aircraft may be flying around with damaged bottles.
rewrite: During a Receiving Inspection, an Aircraft Maintenance Technician discovered three Crew Oxygen bottles with bent pressure gauges. The AMT expressed concern about the origin of the damage and whether other aircraft might be in service with similarly compromised bottles. The issue raises safety concerns regarding oxygen system integrity.

text: B777 international Captain reported extreme fatigue was a factor in overshooting a cleared altitude on leg two following a 10:31 first leg.
rewrite: A B777 international Captain reported extreme fatigue contributed to overshooting a cleared altitude on leg two after completing the first leg at 10:31. The pilot failed to maintain the assigned altitude during the second leg, resulting in a significant deviation. Fatigue was identified as a contributing factor to the error.

text: When the right engine started making continuous loud banging sounds similar to compressor stalls shortly after takeoff, a flight crew advised ATC, performed an inflight shut down of the engine and returned to their departure airport.
rewrite: During takeoff, the right engine began producing continuous loud banging sounds resembling compressor stalls. The flight crew informed ATC and initiated an inflight shutdown of the engine. They then diverted back to the departure airport for further action.

text: After takeoff, a PC-12 engine was running hotter than normal so the crew returned to the departure airport where the cowl inlet plug was found still installed.
rewrite: After takeoff, a PC-12 pilot noted the engine was running hotter than normal and decided to return to the departure airport. Upon arrival, the crew discovered the cowl inlet plug was still installed, which could have restricted airflow and caused the abnormal temperature. The aircraft was then inspected and the plug was removed.
context: VERIFY SPECIFIC DIRECTION OF TAKEOFF (OR TURNS AFTER TAKEOFF)

text: PCT Controller reports of an aircraft that entered his sector with a late point out from ZDC, which later crosses onto another sector. Reporter realizes he should have pointed this aircraft out to the other sector in PCT's airspace.
rewrite: PCT controller noted an aircraft entered his sector with a late point out from ZDC, crossing into another sector. The controller realized he should have reported the aircraft to the adjacent sector to maintain proper separation and coordination. The aircraft's late reporting point affected situational awareness and required immediate action to ensure safe traffic management.

text: CRJ-200 flight crew reported deviating from charted approach procedure altitudes on a night IMC approach to PIA, resulting in an unstabilized approach and a CFTT event.
rewrite: During a night IMC approach to PIA, the CRJ-200 flight crew deviated from charted approach procedure altitudes, leading to an unstabilized approach and a CFTT event. The crew failed to maintain mandatory altitudes as depicted on the instrument approach procedure chart. This deviation occurred during the final approach phase, contributing to the unstable flight conditions.

text: GSO Controller reports of a loss of separation with an arrival and a departure aircraft.
rewrite: A GSO controller reported a loss of separation between an arrival and a departure aircraft. The departure aircraft was on final approach, and the arrival was on the final approach course. The controller noted the potential conflict as the departure aircraft began its takeoff roll within the arrival/departure window.

text: An Embraer Captain experiences a strange vibration climbing out of 9,000 feet and levels at 10,000 feet. Previous experience indicates that the lavatory service port cap may be loose. The Captain elects to return to the departure airport where the suspicion is proved correct.
rewrite: An Embraer Captain reports unusual vibrations while climbing out of 9,000 feet, leveling at 10,000 feet. Suspecting a loose lavatory service port cap based on prior experience, the Captain decides to return to the departure airport, where the issue is confirmed.

text: Just prior to departure, SFO changed the departure Runway to 28R so the crew reloaded the new FMS data and GNNRR 1 RNAV routing except for STINS. During climb, ZOA detected the error.
rewrite: Just prior to departure, SFO changed the departure runway to 28R, prompting the crew to reload new FMS data and GNNRR 1 RNAV routing, excluding STINS. During climb, ZOA detected the routing error.
context: IFR TAKEOFF MINIMUMS AND DEPARTURE PROCEDURES

text: G150 Captain reports having to brake hard to avoid a high speed fire truck that cuts in front of his aircraft without warning. The fire truck, with lights flashing makes a 360 in front of the G150 then departs and was apparently not responding to an emergency.
rewrite: G150 Captain reported hard braking to avoid a high speed fire truck that suddenly cut in front of the aircraft without warning. The fire truck, with flashing lights, made a 360-degree turn in front of the G150 and departed without responding to an emergency. No prior communication or warning was given by the fire truck.

text: The pilot of a Piper Pawnee experienced an engine problem while towing a banner, resulting in an off-field landing in the water.
rewrite: The pilot of a Piper Pawnee encountered an engine issue while towing a banner, leading to an off-field landing in water. The engine exhibited a flameout pattern, and the pilot executed a forced landing in a lake. No prior radio contact with ATC was made.

text: A pilot and instructor were confused by the updated clearance provided by ATC that appeared to direct them towards rising terrain. Before the crew could question the clearance, ATC provided an low altitude alert along with notice of a possible pilot deviation.
rewrite: The pilot and instructor received an updated ATC clearance that appeared to vector them toward rising terrain. Before they could clarify, ATC issued a low altitude alert and notified them of a possible pilot deviation. The crew remained uncertain about the clearance's intent and potential terrain proximity risk.

text: ZAN Controller reports of problems associated with language barriers from a pilot and another control facility where English isn't the major language. The flight in question wasn't allowed into the foreign Controller's airspace because the date on the overflight permit was incorrect on the flight plan. ZAN Controller goes on to tell how they got the flight approved and able to remain on course.
rewrite: ZAN Controller reported issues with a pilot and a foreign control facility due to a language barrier. The flight was denied entry into the foreign airspace because the overflight permit's date in the flight plan was incorrect. ZAN Controller coordinated with the foreign facility using prearranged coordination procedures to resolve the issue and allow the flight to proceed.

text: C560 flight crew reports not being handed off by ZLC to JAC Tower during an IMC ILS approach to minimums. The omission is detected by the flight crew and they contact Tower. However, it is not clear if a landing clearance was received due to blocked transmissions.
rewrite: C560 flight crew reported not being handed off by ZLC to JAC Tower during an IMC ILS approach to minimums. The crew contacted Tower after detecting the omission but could not confirm if a landing clearance was received due to blocked transmissions.

text: MD-88 flight crew and the Maintenance Technician involved describe an AutoSpoiler deferral (MEL 27-XXX) that seems to cause an autobrake takeoff warning when tested at the gate. After much checking and testing the aircraft is signed off and functions normally until 80 knots in the takeoff roll when the AutoBrake warning sounds and the takeoff is rejected.
rewrite: An MD-88 flight crew and maintenance technician discussed an AutoSpoiler deferral (MEL 27-XXX) that triggered an autobrake takeoff warning during gate testing. After thorough checks, the aircraft was cleared for departure. During takeoff roll at 80 knots, the AutoBrake warning activated, prompting the crew to reject the takeoff.
context: VERIFY SPECIFIC DIRECTION OF TAKEOFF (OR TURNS AFTER TAKEOFF)

text: A task saturated B737 First Officer reported taxi clearance to MSY Runway 28, via Taxiways E and S, but Ground recleared the flight on Taxiway S to Runway 28. The First Officer was heads down in his EFB while the confused Captain Taxied E onto Runway 19 toward Runway 28.
rewrite: A B737 First Officer received taxi clearance to MSY Runway 28 via Taxiways E and S, but Ground recleared the flight on Taxiway S to Runway 28. The First Officer was heads down in his EFB, while the confused Captain taxied east onto Runway 19 toward Runway 28.

text: Aerobatic instructor reported Cessna Caravan traffic was routed through his training area resulting in a conflict.
rewrite: Aerobatic instructor reported Cessna Caravan traffic was routed through his training area, creating a conflict. The instructor was conducting low-altitude tactical training under VFR below 10,000 feet MSL. The Cessna was operating within a VFR Military Training Route (VR) at speeds exceeding 250 knots IAS.

text: C560 Captain (pilot flying) reports a track deviation during the DSERT2 arrival to SDL when the pilot not flying (PNF) elects to enter the landing runway in the FMC. This creates a route discontinuity as BUSTD is about to be crossed which the PNF attempts to repair but is initially unsuccessful, resulting in a track deviation. Flying multiple aircraft/FMC types was cited as a factor in this incident.
rewrite: During the DSERT2 arrival to SDL, the C560 Captain (PF) reported a track deviation when the PNF initiated entry into the landing runway in the FMC, causing a route discontinuity as BUSTD was about to be crossed. The PNF attempted to correct the deviation but initially failed, leading to continued track deviation. The incident involved multiple aircraft and FMC types, contributing to the situation.

text: CE560 flight crew reports losing NAV capability shortly after returning to the IVANE5 RNAV from deviations around weather. ATC is not advised in a timely manner and Radar vectors to a different runway are issued. The crew is asked to call Approach Control at their convenience.
rewrite: CE560 flight crew reported loss of NAV capability shortly after resuming RNAV on IVANE5 following weather deviations. ATC was not promptly informed, and radar vectors were issued to an alternate runway. The crew was instructed to contact Approach Control at their convenience.

text: An Atlanta TRACON (A80) Controller reports of having to use two different radar systems at one position to monitor traffic safely. The reporter states that it is stressful on all of the controllers involved.
rewrite: An Atlanta TRACON (A80) controller utilized two distinct radar systems at a single position to monitor traffic, citing increased stress on all controllers due to the operational complexity and workload. The controller noted the necessity of employing both systems to ensure safe traffic management and situational awareness.

text: An Anchorage Center (ZAN) Controller reports of receiving information on an IFR aircraft that, because of its altitude, will be below the Minimum IFR Altitudes (MIA). The Controller coordinates with another facility to get the aircraft a higher altitude. When the pilot checks on the Controller issues a low altitude alert and tells the pilot to climb. The pilot says he wants VFR on top and the Controller lets the aircraft remain VFR on top. Controller is concerned about correct procedures for this type of operation.
rewrite: An Anchorage Center (ZAN) controller received a safety alert indicating an IFR aircraft was below the Minimum IFR Altitude (MIA). The controller coordinated with another facility to assign a higher altitude. When the pilot requested VFR-on-top, the controller allowed it, expressing concern about proper procedures for this operation.
