text: ROW Tower Controller and pilot reported of landing at ROW on a closed runway.
rewrite: ROW Tower Controller and pilot reported landing on a closed runway. The pilot initiated a circle-to-land maneuver after ATC authorization. The approach runway verification system alerted controllers that the aircraft was not aligned with the assigned runway.

text: Lear 45 flight crew reported an uncontrolled climb to FL412 from FL400 as a result of moderate to severe turbulence.
rewrite: During cruise climb, the Lear 45 flight crew experienced moderate to severe turbulence, resulting in an uncontrolled climb from FL400 to FL412. The turbulence caused significant changes in altitude and attitude, prompting the crew to report the incident as a PILOT’S DISCRETION event. The turbulence was consistent with SIGMET advisories for severe turbulence.

text: An A320 was being pushed at dusk in a confined area when one of its Sharklet wingtips hit a B757 tail because the wing walker did not warn of the collision and also the new wingtips are very high off the ground.
rewrite: An A320 was being pushed at dusk in a confined area when a Sharklet wingtip struck a B757 tail. The incident occurred because the wing walker failed to warn of the collision. The new wingtips were unusually high off the ground, contributing to the close proximity between the aircraft.
context: NORTH ATLANTIC HIGH LEVEL AIRSPACE (NAT HLA)
TRAFFIC ALERT AND COLLISION AVOIDANCE SYSTEM (TCAS)

text: A320 Captain reported concern about an MEL on the fleet that allows aircraft to be dispatched with the cockpit access keypad inoperative, since that would preclude any emergency access to the cockpit.
rewrite: A320 Captain expressed concern regarding an MEL item permitting dispatch with the cockpit access keypad inoperative, which would prevent emergency access to the cockpit. The issue relates to cockpit security and safety during emergencies. The captain emphasized the potential risk associated with this inoperative keypad.

text: A319 crew experienced an overheating engine warning and were able to resolve the issue before landing. Overheat warning reoccurred during taxi, resulting in cancellation of the next flight after the crew encountered communication difficulties with Dispatch and Maintenance Control.
rewrite: An A319 crew received an engine overheating warning during flight, which they resolved before landing. The warning reoccurred during taxi, prompting communication issues with Dispatch and Maintenance Control, leading to cancellation of the subsequent flight. The crew encountered difficulties in coordinating with maintenance and dispatch teams.
context: EN ROUTE MINIMUM SAFE ALTITUDE WARNING (E

text: A Large Transport Aircraft was high on the SILCN 1 arrival profile because the ILS 30 transition point is GILRO which occurs after the common SILCN 1 to ILS 30 transition point KLIDE. Therefore the FMC will fly from KLIDE to GILRO to KLIDE which requires the additional altitude.
rewrite: A Large Transport Aircraft was high on the SILCN 1 arrival profile because the ILS 30 transition point is GILRO, which occurs after the common SILCN 1 to ILS 30 transition point KLIDE. As a result, the FMC flew from KLIDE to GILRO to KLIDE, requiring an additional altitude due to the extended path.

text: Pilot of R-22 momentarily lost control while attempting to retrieve an airport diagram, resulting in some aircraft damage.
rewrite: Pilot of R-22 momentarily lost control while attempting to retrieve an airport diagram, resulting in some aircraft damage. The loss of control was brief, and the aircraft did not enter a flyaway mode. No communication loss or link interruption was reported.

text: During pushback, a tug crew failed to push the aircraft to the proper location and disconnected the tow bar before obtaining clearance from the flight crew. The aircraft momentarily began to roll before the flight crew applied brakes.
rewrite: During pushback, the tug crew failed to position the aircraft correctly and disconnected the tow bar without obtaining clearance from the flight crew. The aircraft began to move forward momentarily before the flight crew applied brakes to stop it.

text: C208 Amphibian flight crew reported landing in FLL with the gear up, following a go-around that was directed by ATC. During the go-around, the flight crew encountered wake turbulence from a departing A320.
rewrite: A C208 Amphibian crew landed at FLL with gear up after a go-around initiated by ATC. During the go-around, they experienced wake turbulence from a departing A320. The turbulence occurred as the A320 was operating directly behind the C208.

text: Taylorcraft pilot reported severe wake turbulence and loss of aircraft control in 6-mile trail of an A319 at CID.
rewrite: A Taylorcraft pilot experienced severe wake turbulence and lost aircraft control while flying 6 miles behind an A319 at CID. The turbulence occurred during the approach phase, leading to a loss of control. The pilot reported the incident to ATC, noting the significant impact of the wake turbulence from the preceding aircraft.

text: On final visual approach, C-172 crew on a CFI training flight experienced a NMAC with a crop duster also on final approach. Crew executed a go-around, re-entered the traffic pattern and landed.
rewrite: On final visual approach, a C-172 training flight encountered a near mid-air collision (NMAC) with a crop duster also on final approach. The crew executed a go-around, re-entered the traffic pattern, and completed a straight-in approach to land.

text: A pilot departing FFZ reported a near miss with a UAV at 3,700 feet.
rewrite: A pilot departing the FFZ reported a near miss with a UAV at 3,700 feet. The pilot observed the UAV while maintaining climb and reported the incident to ATC. No further details were provided regarding the UAV's identification or trajectory.

text: An air carrier crew landed on LRD Runway 17R and were cleared to exit at Taxiway D, cross Runways 14 and 17L to the ramp. When the Taxiway D centerline turned right the crew followed it because at night it appeared D ended at 17L and turned. They actually turned on Runway 14.
rewrite: An air carrier crew landed on LRD Runway 17R and were cleared to exit at Taxiway D, cross Runways 14 and 17L to the ramp. Upon exiting Taxiway D, the crew followed the centerline turn right, believing it led to 17L. However, they inadvertently turned onto Runway 14 instead of continuing on Taxiway D.

text: GGG TRACON Controller reports of a loss of separation due to a flight of aircraft that deviated due to weather. The flight had previously cancelled IFR, but could not maintain VFR due to the weather.
rewrite: GGG TRACON controller reported a loss of separation involving an aircraft that deviated from its planned route due to adverse weather. The flight had previously cancelled IFR but was unable to maintain VFR conditions, leading to a deviation. The controller noted the weather conditions were below VFR minimums, contributing to the loss of separation.

text: The flight crew reported that they were unable to control the cabin pressurization. Several lower altitudes were requested from ATC until the aircraft leveled at 10,000 feet. The cabin altitude never exceeded 9,200 feet and a normal approach and landing was accomplished.
rewrite: The flight crew reported inability to control cabin pressurization. They requested several lower altitudes from ATC until leveling off at 10,000 feet MSL. Cabin altitude remained below 9,200 feet, allowing for a normal approach and landing.

text: EMB-145 First Officer reported departing, at the direction of the Captain, without required ballast to correct a CG problem.
rewrite: First Officer of an EMB-145 reported departing without required ballast as directed by the Captain to correct a center of gravity issue. The action was taken to ensure proper aircraft balance during the takeoff phase. No correction was made to the ballast configuration prior to departure.

text: A320 flight crew failed to obtain a new/amended release and had to declare minimum fuel for landing.
rewrite: A320 flight crew failed to obtain a route amendment dialog (RAD) and had to declare minimum fuel for landing due to unanticipated route changes affecting their fuel planning. The crew did not receive updated routing information, leading to a fuel shortfall at the destination. They declared minimum fuel to ensure a safe landing with the available fuel.

text: B737 Captain reported that during pushback he was almost hit by the aircraft being pushed off the adjacent gate.
rewrite: During pushback, the B737 captain nearly collided with an aircraft being pushed off the adjacent gate. The incident occurred as the captain was maneuvering the aircraft backward from the gate. No specific ATC instructions or procedures were mentioned in the report.

text: A319 Captain reported a track deviation on takeoff from ATL when, just prior to takeoff, they received a last minute change to their clearance that involved a turn at the middle marker. Reporter indicated he could not locate the middle marker.
rewrite: During takeoff from ATL, the A319 Captain experienced a track deviation after receiving a last-minute clearance change requiring a turn at the middle marker. The pilot reported being unable to locate the middle marker, which is part of the ILS system, indicating a potential navigation issue during the departure phase.

text: Air carrier Dispatcher reported a possible hazardous materials violation.
rewrite: An air carrier dispatcher identified a potential hazardous materials violation, notifying the appropriate authorities. The incident involved a scheduled air carrier operation, prompting an investigation into compliance with 49 CFR §171.8. The dispatcher's report initiated a review of the cargo manifest and loading procedures.

text: Houston TRACON (I90) reports of having to vector and climb aircraft off of final due to weather. The reporter stated that they received no help from Traffic Management Unit (TMU) as this developed into a loss of separation.
rewrite: Houston TRACON (I90) vectored and instructed aircraft to climb off final approach due to weather. The pilot reported no assistance from the Traffic Management Unit (TMU) as the situation led to a loss of separation. The controller noted the need for immediate action to maintain safe spacing.

text: A flight instructor with 2 students became distracted and started the engine with the tow bar still attached to the nose landing gear of a Piper Cherokee, causing damage to the propeller.
rewrite: A flight instructor, during a training flight, became distracted and initiated an airstart with the tow bar still connected to the Piper Cherokee's nose landing gear. The feathered propeller sustained damage due to the unexpected movement. The instructor failed to notice the tow bar attachment before starting the engine.

text: A C560XL Captain reported pitch trim problems that caused an upset at FL280. The flight diverted to a suitable alternate.
rewrite: A C560XL captain experienced pitch trim issues resulting in an aircraft upset at FL280. The pilot diverted to a suitable alternate aerodrome due to the trim problems. The flight proceeded to land at the alternate without further incident.

text: CE560 pilot reported it took heavy back pressure to rotate on takeoff, and later determined the set screws securing the trim indicator had come loose, affecting the stabilizer trim operation.
rewrite: CE560 pilot reported heavy back pressure during rotation, later discovering loose set screws on the trim indicator, which impacted stabilizer trim function during takeoff. The issue affected pitch control, requiring manual adjustment to maintain flight path. The trim system's integrity was compromised due to the loose set screws.

text: CRJ200 Captain reported climbing above 10000 feet with the autopilot engaged in vertical speed mode. When the PFD is checked the airspeed is approaching 220 knots.
rewrite: The CRJ200 captain climbed above 10,000 feet with the autopilot in vertical speed mode. Upon checking the PFD, the airspeed was approaching 220 knots. The pilot noted the airspeed was increasing despite the autopilot's engagement.

text: A Lancair LNC4 door window developed a six inch crack at FL240 and depressurized. The pilot had difficulty keeping his oxygen cannula on his face in place and calling ATC for a lower altitude but he was ultimately successful.
rewrite: A Lancair LNC4 experienced a six-inch crack in its door window at FL240, leading to depressurization. The pilot struggled to maintain his oxygen cannula during the emergency descent mode activation. He successfully contacted ATC for a lower altitude and initiated a descent to regain cabin pressure.

text: ZJX Controller reports of a scenario where he used emergency authority for an aircraft that had to enter a Warning Area due to weather. The Controller tried other options but none were safe except for the aircraft to fly into the Warning Area. Controller was later told by management that the pilot should have been the one to use emergency authority.
rewrite: ZJX controller utilized emergency authority to direct an aircraft into a warning area due to severe weather, after exhausting other options. The controller attempted alternative routes but found them unsafe. Management later indicated the pilot should have initiated emergency authority instead.
context: EN ROUTE MINIMUM SAFE ALTITUDE WARNING (E

text: B737 Captain reported he attempted to set the parking brake after push back but did not notice the Parking Brake Light was not on after the attempt.
rewrite: A B737 captain attempted to set the parking brake during push back but failed to notice the parking brake light remained off, indicating the brake was not engaged. The pilot did not observe any indication the parking brake had been activated. No braking action advisories were mentioned in the report.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: RV8 pilot departing OSH reported an NMAC with an aircraft arriving on the FISK arrival.
rewrite: RV8 pilot departing OSH reported an NMAC with an aircraft arriving on the FISK arrival. The incident occurred during the departure phase, with the departing aircraft in the arrival/departure window. The arriving aircraft was on the final approach course, creating a potential conflict.

text: Jetstar First Officer experienced an unnoticed autopilot disconnect at FL360 with the Captain in the lavatory. The aircraft is recovered from a 45 degree bank at FL330 and ATC is advised. The autopilot is reengaged and functions normally for the remainder of the flight.
rewrite: Jetstar First Officer noticed an autopilot disconnect at FL360 while the Captain was in the lavatory. The aircraft entered a 45-degree bank at FL330, prompting ATC advisement. Autopilot was reengaged and functioned normally for the remainder of the flight.

text: Dash 8 flight crew reported they shut down the #1 engine in flight because of low oil pressure. Flight diverted to a suitable nearby alternate.
rewrite: Dash 8 flight crew shut down #1 engine during cruise due to low oil pressure. They diverted to a suitable nearby alternate aerodrome as per procedures. The aircraft remained airborne and operational with remaining engines.

text: B737-700 Captain reported uncommanded 45 degree roll from preceding aircraft wake on approach to Runway 9R at ATL.
rewrite: A B737-700 captain experienced an uncommanded 45-degree roll while on approach to Runway 9R at ATL, attributed to wake turbulence from a preceding aircraft. The roll occurred during the final approach phase, consistent with the SAME DIRECTION AIRCRAFT criteria. The aircraft was operating in the same direction, with tracks intersecting at less than 45 degrees.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: A light twin Flight Instructor experienced a gear up landing while instructing. Preparations for a no flap landing and an ATC assigned runway change may have gotten in the way of completing the landing check.
rewrite: A light twin flight instructor experienced a gear-up landing during a training session. The instructor had prepared for a no-flap landing, but an ATC-assigned runway change may have disrupted the completion of the landing check. The incident occurred during the landing phase.

text: A Flight Attendant reported that ramp personnel were not accepting oversized bags during boarding. When confronted with policy and FAR violations, the lack of ramp management oversight and lack of ramp employee concern for their actions' consequences was cause for concern.
rewrite: A flight attendant reported that ramp personnel were refusing to accept oversized bags during boarding. Despite being informed of policy and FAR violations, ramp management showed no oversight, and employees displayed no concern for the consequences of their actions. This lack of accountability raised safety concerns.

text: A pilot flying near Windham High Peak in Greene County New York, at 3,500 feet was approached by an elaborate UAV with a brilliant surface on top of an inverted bowl shaped container with long rectangular antennas protruding downward. The UAV approached, tracked, and flew around the reporter before speeding off toward the west with two other like shaped UAVs.
rewrite: A pilot flying near Windham High Peak, NY, at 3,500 feet encountered an elaborate UAV with a brilliant surface on top of an inverted bowl-shaped container and long rectangular antennas. The UAV approached, tracked, and circled the aircraft before accelerating westward with two similar UAVs. The encounter occurred during cruise phase.
context: TERMINAL-VERY HIGH FREQUENCY OMNIDIRECTIONAL RANGE STATION (TVOR)

text: An air carrier Captain discovered while climbing to cruise from ABQ that the passenger manifest count was off and the aircraft weight was off by 5,800 pounds making the actual takeoff weight heavier than what was shown on the loading schedule.
rewrite: During the cruise climb phase from ABQ, the captain noticed a discrepancy in the passenger manifest count, resulting in an actual aircraft weight 5,800 pounds heavier than the maximum gross operating weight indicated on the loading schedule. This discrepancy affected the takeoff weight, requiring adjustments to ensure compliance with weight and balance limitations.

text: An MD-11 crew returned to the departure airport after experiencing an 'EMER PWR ON' event with an associated battery discharge.
rewrite: An MD-11 crew executed a return to the departure airport following an 'EMER PWR ON' event, which triggered an associated battery discharge during the en route phase of the flight. The crew initiated a diversion to the original departure airport due to the emergency power system activation and subsequent battery discharge. The flight was conducted under a ROUND flight plan, with the crew managing the situation without further complications.

text: A solo corporate jet pilot's tablet overheated in the sunlight during vectors to EWR. He switched tablets but it too overheated. During this time he was slowing to comply with an ATC request. Finally, the initial tablet became operational and remained out of sunlight.
rewrite: A solo corporate jet pilot experienced tablet overheating during vectors to EWR due to sunlight exposure. After switching tablets, the second one also overheated. During this period, the pilot was slowing to comply with an ATC request. The initial tablet eventually became operational once moved out of sunlight.

text: While climbing over the Western Pacific between 16,000 feet and FL260 with thunderstorms in the area, a B737 Captain's altimeter was intermittently fluctuating so the flight returned to the departure airport on the advice of Maintenance.
rewrite: While climbing over the Western Pacific between 16,000 feet and FL260, a B737 captain reported intermittent altimeter fluctuations due to thunderstorms in the area. The flight was advised to return to the departure airport by Maintenance. The crew executed a visual climb over the airport (VCOA) to descend and rejoin the departure airport.

text: B737-800 flight crew reported right fuel tank 'LOW PRESS' lights illuminated and right engine spooled down and restarted several times during descent and landing.
rewrite: During descent and landing, the B737-800 flight crew observed the right fuel tank 'LOW PRESS' lights illuminated. The right engine experienced multiple spool-down events, requiring restarts. The crew managed the situation without further incident.

text: B737-800 flight crew reported they failed to make a crossing restriction on the RNAV Y Arrival to MDW when they got distracted with late runway change programming.
rewrite: During the RNAV Y Arrival to MDW, the B737-800 flight crew failed to comply with a crossing restriction at a specified fix due to distraction caused by late runway condition code programming. The crew did not cross the fix at or above the assigned altitude, resulting in a deviation from the published procedure. The error occurred during the approach phase while managing runway change inputs.

text: The reporter states that aircraft repeatedly climb to 12,000 feet on their airports' SID but are supposed to be climbing to 16,000 feet. The SID assigned altitude is 12,000 feet.
rewrite: Aircraft repeatedly climbed to 12,000 feet on their airport's SID, but were expected to climb to 16,000 feet. The SID assigned altitude was 12,000 feet, leading to a discrepancy in climb instructions. Pilots reported climbing to the assigned altitude, but the required climb was not achieved.

text: Three different ARTCC sectors working three aircraft in confliction with each other. Very confusing scenario due to the different sectors taking point out coordination with different intentions to resolving the traffic conflictions instead of one controller working the aircraft with one plan for separation.
rewrite: Three aircraft in conflict within different ARTCC sectors caused confusion as each sector pursued separate coordination efforts. Instead of a unified plan for separation, controllers applied varying intentions to resolve the traffic conflictions, leading to unclear lateral spacing and potential safety risks. The situation highlighted the need for strategic planning and coordinated conflict resolution across sectors.

text: Crew of a Challenger 300 was cleared for ILS approach to 31C at MDW and to maintain 210 knots until RUNTS, a fix 6.7 miles from the localizer. The crew believed that flying the glideslope from their current position would require them to fly below the Class B airspace, which has a floor of 3600 feet in this area. Crew asked ATC about the clearance to violate the FAR restriction of airspeed below 200 knots below Class B airspace. ATC confirmed the 210-knot clearance, the crew elected to maintain 200 knots as required by FAR 91.117(c).
rewrite: Crew of a Challenger 300 was cleared for ILS approach to Runway 31C at MDW and to maintain 210 knots until RUNTS, a fix 6.7 miles from the localizer. The crew believed flying the glideslope from their current position would require them to fly below Class B airspace, which has a floor of 3600 feet. They asked ATC about clearance to violate FAR 91.117(c) by flying below 200 knots in Class B. ATC confirmed the 21

text: A Finals sector at Atlanta Approach became extremely busy. Due to weather deviations this sector was being fed more aircraft than planned for by the Traffic Management Program and controllers. The sector was receiving aircraft at high speeds and insufficiently sequenced. The controller advised the supervisor of the situation. The controller was to be relieved from the sector but felt they were too busy to take the time to give a new controller a briefing. The controller felt the supervisor was not responding to his requests for spacing from the sectors feeding him. The controller advised the supervisor he would not accept any more aircraft handoffs to his sector. Another controller was sent to relieve him but he felt too busy to give a complete briefing. The relieving controller assumed the position after observing for a while.
rewrite: A Finals sector at Atlanta Approach became extremely busy due to weather deviations, resulting in more aircraft than planned being fed into the sector. Controllers faced high-speed, insufficiently sequenced traffic and requested spacing from upstream sectors without success. The controller refused further aircraft handoffs and delayed briefing a relieving controller, who eventually took over after observing the sector.

text: A ZID Controller reported a wind farm that is giving a weather presentation on Enroute Automation Modernization at the center. The display was showing weather over an area of about 100 by 60 miles. NWS was also getting the display on their equipment. Controller's aircraft data tags are not highly visible when in the area.
rewrite: A ZID controller noted a wind farm providing a weather presentation during Enroute Automation Modernization. The WIND GRID DISPLAY showed weather over a 100 by 60-mile area, with NWS also receiving the data. The controller's aircraft data tags were not clearly visible in the region.

text: A320 Captain reports receiving a gate change after landing then having to wait for outbound traffic before being cleared in. Before reaching the gate, airport personnel painting lines on the ramp along with their vehicles are blocking further progress. Once vehicles and personnel are clear and wing walkers have arrived, the Marshall directs the aircraft into the gate only to have to stop abruptly to avoid a truck dashing through the gap.
rewrite: A320 Captain reports a gate change after landing, followed by a wait for outbound traffic before being cleared to taxi in. While approaching the gate, airport personnel and vehicles painting lines on the ramp block progress. After clearance and wing walker arrival, the Marshall directs the aircraft into the gate, but it stops abruptly to avoid a truck entering the gap.

text: Cessna 402C pilot reported losing his attitude indicator shortly after takeoff in IMC.
rewrite: A Cessna 402C pilot reported losing the attitude indicator shortly after takeoff in IMC conditions. The pilot was unable to determine aircraft attitude, leading to difficulty maintaining altitude and airspeed. The aircraft was in the climb phase, and the pilot requested vectors to the nearest VOR for navigation.

text: B767-300ER flight crew reported receiving MAIN BAT CHARGER EICAS message, so they diverted to a nearby suitable airport.
rewrite: The B767-300ER flight crew received a MAIN BAT CHARGER EICAS message and decided to divert to a nearby suitable airport for further assessment and maintenance. The crew acknowledged the message and initiated the diversion procedure without delay. No other anomalies were reported during the flight.

text: Air carrier cargo handler questioned the safety aspects of a new company procedure that requires that the cargo belt-loader not be placed inside the cargo pit.
rewrite: A cargo handler at an air carrier facility raised concerns about the safety of a new procedure mandating that the cargo belt-loader remain outside the cargo pit during loading operations. The handler questioned the potential risks associated with this change, particularly regarding visibility and access during the loading process. The procedure was implemented to enhance operational efficiency, but the handler emphasized the need for a thorough safety assessment.

text: Q400 Captain reported an altitude deviation that stemmed from a high workload situation in bad weather.
rewrite: A Q400 captain reported an altitude deviation due to a high workload during adverse weather conditions. The deviation occurred as the crew managed multiple tasks while navigating through turbulent airspace. The pilot indicated the deviation was not intentional but resulted from operational pressures during the approach phase.

text: B747 flight crew reported parking at a gate with a self park system that was providing erratic guidance while they were parking, resulting in an overshoot of the intended stop point.
rewrite: A B747 flight crew reported parking at a gate using a self-park system that provided erratic guidance, leading to an overshoot of the intended stop point. The aircraft exceeded the designated parking position during the parking maneuver. The crew had to manually adjust the aircraft to align with the gate.

text: A B737 Flight Attendant reported severe turbulence at cruise which resulted in a Flight Attendant and passenger needing medical attention immediately after landing. The reporter sought medical aid at home for back, neck and other injuries.
rewrite: A B737 flight attendant reported severe turbulence during cruise, leading to injuries for the attendant and a passenger. The incident required immediate medical attention post-landing. The affected personnel sought medical aid at home for back, neck, and other injuries.

text: A B737 Takeoff Warning Horn alert volume was so low the crew did not identify it until takeoff thrust was set. When the warning was finally identified at about 50 knots, the takeoff was rejected and the aircraft returned to the gate.
rewrite: A B737 crew failed to detect the Takeoff Warning Horn due to its low volume, despite it sounding during the takeoff roll. The alert was recognized at approximately 50 knots, prompting the crew to reject the takeoff and return to the gate. The incident occurred during the initial climb phase.

text: BE58 pilot experiences an alternator failure on a part 135 flight and lands safely at the destination airport. The reporter contacts the Chief Pilot to ensure that a part 91 ferry flight back to base with the alternator inoperative is legal and is told that it is. The flight is uneventful but maintenance informs that the Alternator 'failure' was the result of a broken alternator drive shaft that had fallen back into the engine crank case and caused damage.
rewrite: BE58 pilot reported an alternator failure during a Part 135 flight and landed safely at the destination. The pilot contacted the Chief Pilot to confirm the legality of a Part 91 ferry flight back to base with the alternator inoperative, which was approved. Maintenance later determined the "failure" was caused by a broken alternator drive shaft that fell into the engine crankcase.

text: B737-800 First Officer reported he and the Captain missed a speed restriction departing DTW because of the scale selected on their iPad EFBs.
rewrite: During departure from DTW, the B737-800 First Officer and Captain missed a speed restriction due to the scale selected on their iPad EFBs. The pilots failed to notice the published speed limit as it was not visible on the current display. The crew did not receive a RESUME PUBLISHED SPEED or RESUME NORMAL SPEED instruction from ATC.

text: B757 First Officer experienced a loss of engine oil pressure at FL360 while the Captain was on a bathroom break. Within moments the engine failed and the Captain quickly returned to the cockpit and began reading the QRH. The engine was shut down and the flight diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
rewrite: A B757 First Officer reported a loss of engine oil pressure at FL360 while the Captain was in the lavatory. Moments later, the engine failed, prompting the Captain to return to the cockpit and initiate QRH procedures. The engine was subsequently shut down, and the flight diverted to the nearest suitable airport.

text: Tower Supervisor noticed an aircraft on short final to a closed runway. The Supervisor immediately alerted the Local Controller to issue a go around instruction which they did in a timely manner. The airport had an active intersecting runway at the time. The reporter does not state if the Controller cleared the aircraft to land on the closed runway or if the pilot lined up to the wrong runway and the Controller didn't notice.
rewrite: Tower Supervisor observed an aircraft on short final to a closed runway and promptly alerted the Local Controller, who issued a go-around instruction. The airport had an active intersecting runway, but it is unclear whether the Controller cleared the aircraft to land on the closed runway or if the pilot misaligned with the correct runway without notice.

text: An air carrier flight crew reported encountering significant wind shear while conducting an approach. They executed a missed approach and, due to a critical fuel state, requested a traffic priority and diverted to an alternate airport.
rewrite: An air carrier flight crew encountered significant wind shear during final approach. They executed a missed approach and, due to a critical fuel state, requested traffic priority and diverted to an alternate airport.

text: EMB-175 First Officer reported multiple system issues on short final that resulted in the flight being towed to the gate after landing.
rewrite: During short final approach, the EMB-175 First Officer reported multiple system malfunctions. The crew initiated a landing, but post-landing, the aircraft was towed to the gate due to unresolved issues. The situation occurred during the landing phase with no prior indication of system failures.

text: Small jet First Officer describes the shoddy maintenance practices of the company he works for. An engine that had low oil pressure was 'repaired' and the crew tasked to ferry the aircraft back to base. The engine exhibits high oil pressure and erratic oil temperature in flight and is operated at reduced thrust to return to base. Mechanics removed the oil filter and oil screen revealing large amounts of metal chunks, flakes, and dust and informed the crew that they had cleaned metal from the oil system several times before.
rewrite: A small jet first officer reports shoddy maintenance practices, noting an engine with low oil pressure was 'repaired' and the crew tasked with a ferry flight to base. During the ferry, the engine showed high oil pressure and erratic temperature, prompting reduced thrust. Mechanics had previously removed metal chunks, flakes, and dust from the oil system.

text: Tower Controller advised a landing aircraft to exit the runway 'quickly' so as to expedite departing traffic. The landing aircraft than was switched to Ground Control. Ground Control delayed the arrival's runway exit for their taxiing aircraft. The Airport Movement Area Safety System did not alert. The controllers were not sure if the arriving aircraft was completely clear of the runway prior to the departure taking off.
rewrite: Tower Controller instructed a landing aircraft to exit the runway quickly to expedite departing traffic. The aircraft was then transferred to Ground Control, who delayed the exit for a taxiing aircraft. The Airport Movement Area Safety System did not trigger an alert. Controllers were uncertain if the arriving aircraft was fully clear of the runway before the departure took off.

text: DA900 Captain reported they deviated from their cleared track when their Honeywell Epic equipped aircraft made a wide 'smart turn' during arrival into DAL.
rewrite: DA900's captain reported a lateral deviation from the cleared track during arrival into Dallas Love Field. The Honeywell Epic-equipped aircraft executed a wide 'smart turn,' resulting in a gross navigation error. The deviation occurred as the aircraft attempted to intercept the final approach course.

text: Cessna 208B pilot reported directional control problems during taxi.
rewrite: A Cessna 208B pilot experienced directional control issues while taxiing. The pilot requested assistance from air traffic control due to difficulty maintaining straight-line movement. The situation occurred during the taxi phase, with no indication of a specific runway or location involved.

text: RV12 pilot reported being stuck on top of a cloud layer upon arrival at his destination and called on 121.5 for ATC assistance. ATC provided a vector to an airport with better weather and an IMC descent to VFR conditions. The Controller received high praise.
rewrite: RV12 pilot encountered cloud tops upon arrival and contacted 121.5 for ATC assistance. ATC vectored the aircraft to an airport with better weather and initiated an IMC descent to VFR conditions. The controller received high praise for the assistance provided.

text: The pilot received a TA and leveled off with military aircraft in sight after departing DTS with a clearance from Elgin.
rewrite: The pilot received a traffic advisory (TA) and leveled off with military aircraft in sight after departing DTS with a clearance from Elgin. The pilot was operating in the local traffic area and confirmed traffic in sight to the controller. No further action was required as the clearance remained valid.
context: CLEARANCE VOID IF NOT OFF BY (TIME)

text: Air carrier aircraft was descended form 34,000 feet to 32,000 feet. The aircraft had opposite direction traffic at 33,000 feet that the Controller did not notice or remember. The Assist Controller pointed out the potential confliction to the Radar Controller when the descent clearance was issued. At the time the Radar Controller issued instructions to separate the aircraft, the aircraft were responding to their TCAS/RA.
rewrite: An air carrier aircraft descended from 34,000 feet to 32,000 feet. The controller failed to notice or recall opposite direction traffic at 33,000 feet. The assist controller alerted the radar controller of the potential confliction during the descent clearance. The radar controller then issued separation instructions as the aircraft were responding to TCAS/RA.

text: After landing at IAH, flight crew received taxi instructions that included confusing information concerning construction closures. Received ATIS contained no information on construction or taxiway closures. While taxiing as cleared, the crew received instructions from ATC to stop in order to avoid wet concrete. Airport personnel arrived to assist the crew in clearing the unmarked construction area, which was the filling of several potholes, and continued taxi to their gate.
rewrite: After landing at IAH, the flight crew followed taxi instructions that included conflicting information regarding construction closures. The received ATIS provided no details on construction or taxiway closures. While taxiing as cleared, the crew was instructed by ATC to stop to avoid wet concrete. Airport personnel arrived to assist in clearing the unmarked construction area, which involved filling potholes, and the crew continued taxiing to their gate.

text: A flight instructor in a SR20 reported a fluctuating oil pressure indication that resulted in a turn back towards the departure airport. The indications became more severe and the engine also was reported to be rough running, so the flight was diverted to the closest airport where a successful landing was made.
rewrite: A flight instructor operating a SR20 experienced fluctuating oil pressure indications, leading to a turn back toward the departure airport. As the issue worsened with rough engine running, the flight was diverted to the nearest airport for a successful landing. The pilot did not use RAIS or QNH during the incident.

text: A tractor driver stopped the pushback when a vehicle was observed crossing behind the aircraft while the driver was using a cellphone.
rewrite: A tractor driver halted the pushback after observing a vehicle crossing behind the aircraft, despite the driver being engaged in a phone call. The driver ceased movement to avoid potential conflict, recognizing the risk posed by the unauthorized vehicle entry during the pushback operation.

text: c152 Instructor Pilot was surprised that another aircraft was allowed to land so close behind them that it could have resulted in a ground collision had they been slower exiting the runway.
rewrite: The C152 instructor pilot was surprised that another aircraft was permitted to land so close behind, resulting in a potential ground collision if the preceding aircraft had not exited the runway quickly. The landing roll of the preceding aircraft was unusually short, leaving minimal clearance for the following aircraft to safely vacate the runway. The instructor expressed concern over the proximity and the risk of a runway incursion.

text: A flight crew reported inadvertently taxiing into an ILS critical area due to communication ambiguities with the taxi clearance issued by ATC.
rewrite: A flight crew inadvertently taxiied into an ILS critical area due to communication ambiguities in the taxi clearance issued by ATC. The pilot received a progressive taxi instruction but misinterpreted the route, leading to entry into the movement area without proper clearance. The crew later realized the error after encountering restricted airspace.

text: Flight crew experienced an apparent ground spoiler problem on landing roll out and decide to watch the spoilers closer on landing next leg.
rewrite: During the landing roll out, the flight crew noticed an apparent malfunction of the ground spoilers, prompting them to monitor the spoilers more closely during the next landing approach. The issue did not affect the landing roll distance or deceleration, as the drag chute functioned normally. The crew decided to increase scrutiny of the spoiler system for the subsequent landing.

text: FWA Controller reported of an instance where he pointed out traffic to Local. Local gave an altitude restriction which the Controller accepted and had his aircraft maintain. Moments later a flight of four aircraft depart and are traffic for the point out aircraft, climbing above the limit the Local Controller set. The reporting Controller issued traffic to the point out traffic and separated it from the flight of four. Reporter went on to say the Local Controller was newly certified and that the facility is pushing people through training and certifying them at minimum time.
rewrite: The FWA controller pointed out traffic to Local, who accepted an altitude restriction and had the aircraft maintain it. Moments later, a flight of four departed and became traffic for the point-out aircraft, climbing above the Local's set limit. The reporting controller issued traffic to the point-out aircraft and separated it from the four. The Local controller was newly certified, and the facility was pushing through training and certification at minimum time.

text: Widebody Airbus cargo aircraft flight crew reported diverting to an alternate after being advised they had lost a large panel in the left wheel well area.
rewrite: A widebody Airbus cargo aircraft flight crew reported diverting to an alternate after being advised they had lost a large panel in the left wheel well area. The crew confirmed the loss of a significant panel during a pre-departure inspection. No immediate control issues were reported, but the diversion was initiated as a precautionary measure.

text: A law enforcement helicopter pilot on a Homeland Security mission is informed that he is inside R-6316. However, he is using a Garmin 430 to avoid the airspace.
rewrite: A law enforcement helicopter pilot on a Homeland Security mission is advised he is within R-6316. He uses a Garmin 430 to navigate around the airspace. The pilot confirms negative contact with the airspace boundary.

text: R44 pilot reported a headset fell from the aircraft during a doors-off tour flight.
rewrite: During a doors-off tour flight, a R44 pilot reported that a headset fell from the aircraft. The incident occurred while the aircraft was in the cruise phase. The pilot did not report any loss of control or other anomalies.

text: The Tower Controller asked the TRACON to break an aircraft out because there was insufficient spacing with the preceding aircraft. The TRACON Controller refused and told the Tower Controller to break the first aircraft out. After the second aircraft contacted the Tower, the Tower issued a go-around instruction and put the aircraft back on the TRACON frequency.
rewrite: The Tower Controller requested the TRACON to break an aircraft out due to insufficient spacing with the preceding aircraft. The TRACON Controller declined and instructed the Tower to break the first aircraft out. Following the second aircraft's contact with the Tower, the Tower issued a go-around and reconnected the aircraft to the TRACON frequency.

text: B737-700 flight crew configured flaps to briefed position late in the approach just before touchdown.
rewrite: Flight crew of a B737-700 configured flaps to the briefed position late in the approach, just before touchdown, during the final phase of the instrument approach. The self-briefing included flap settings for the approach speed and touchdown zone considerations. Flap configuration was delayed, impacting the approach profile and landing performance.

text: CRJ-900 flight crew reported a heading deviation occurred when the pilot not flying misunderstood the pilot flying's request.
rewrite: During departure, the pilot flying requested the pilot not flying to say heading, but the pilot not flying misinterpreted the instruction, resulting in a heading deviation. The pilot flying then corrected the heading, ensuring the aircraft remained on the intended runway heading. The deviation was not authorized and required immediate correction to maintain safe separation.

text: Aircrew used non-standard methods to clean wing surfaces of snow.
rewrite: Aircrew employed non-standard procedures to remove snow from the airplane's wing surfaces during the approach phase. The irregular surface conditions, combined with precipitation, necessitated manual de-icing efforts. Standard de-icing equipment was not utilized, leading to potential performance degradation.

text: BD700 Captain reported an NMAC with a small aircraft on departure at BFI.
rewrite: BD700's captain reported a near mid-air collision (NMAC) with a small aircraft during departure from BFI. The incident occurred while the aircraft was in the initial climb phase. The captain issued a position report indicating proximity to the other aircraft.

text: A pilot reported an airborne conflict during a government contracted animal vaccine dropping flight that required grid pattern operations. Notification of the operation had not been disseminated to an associated agency.
rewrite: During a government contracted animal vaccine dropping flight, a pilot reported an airborne conflict while conducting grid pattern operations. The notification of the operation was not disseminated to an associated agency, leading to potential coordination issues. The conflict was detected by Automated Problem Detection (APD) and alerted to the involved positions.
context: LOW ALTITUDE AUTHORIZATION AND NOTIFICATION CAPABILITY (LAANC)

text: A B777 First Officer described his company's inhospitable crew rest bunk conditions which are not conducive to sleep and result in flight crew fatigue during the flight's final stages.
rewrite: A B777 First Officer reported inadequate crew rest bunk conditions during the flight's final stages, leading to crew fatigue. The bunk's uncomfortable setup hindered sleep, impacting alertness and performance. The issue is company-wide, affecting rest and safety during critical phases of flight.

text: B787 First Officer reported his rest was interrupted by noises from a galley cart that was parked next to the bunk room door.
rewrite: The B787 First Officer reported that his rest was interrupted by noises emanating from a galley cart located adjacent to the bunk room door during the pre-flight preparation phase. The disturbance occurred while the crew was conducting final checks prior to departure. No further action was required as the noise did not affect flight operations.

text: Ramp air carrier employee reported loading a radioactive box with other bags because it was not indicated as radioactive on his information document.
rewrite: A ramp air carrier employee loaded a radioactive box among other bags during baggage handling, as the radioactive designation was not noted on the information document provided. The box was not flagged as hazardous, leading to potential safety concerns during loading. The employee was unaware of the box's radioactive nature at the time of loading.

text: The Local Controller did not notice an aircraft entering downwind was in close proximity to another aircraft already on downwind. Due to workload the Controller had requested an assist position to help them but the request was denied.
rewrite: The local controller failed to notice an aircraft entering downwind was in close proximity to another aircraft already on downwind. Due to workload, the controller had requested an assist position but the request was denied.
context: EN ROUTE AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL SERVICES

text: C310 pilot reported an NMAC at 9,000 FT while on an IFR flight.
rewrite: A Cessna 310 pilot reported a near mid-air collision (NMAC) at 9,000 feet during an IFR flight. The pilot was operating under instrument flight rules and was not in formation flight. No compulsory reporting points were mentioned, and the pilot did not provide a pilot weather report.

text: B737 flight crew received a cancel takeoff clearance and hold short of intersecting runway for landing traffic. Captain did not reject and continued the takeoff because he determined the aircraft would stop in the middle of the intersecting runway. Landing aircraft was instructed to go-around.
rewrite: The B737 flight crew received a cancel takeoff and hold short of intersecting runway clearance for landing traffic. The captain chose not to reject the takeoff, believing the aircraft could stop midway on the intersecting runway. The landing aircraft was subsequently instructed to execute a go-around.

text: HS-125-800 First Officer reported the pilot flying (Captain) continued the approach even though it was unstabilized and the First Officer called for a go-around.
rewrite: The pilot flying (Captain) of HS-125-800 continued the approach despite it being unstabilized. The First Officer called for a go-around, but the Captain did not comply, leading to a potential safety concern during the approach phase.

text: A fuel cap retaining chain was disconnected and the cap was found on the wing of the aircraft. When deicing, the cap was knocked off the wing. Maintenance reinstalled the cap.
rewrite: During deicing, a fuel cap retained by a disconnected chain was dislodged from the wing. The cap was later found on the wing and subsequently reinstalled by maintenance. No fuel was released, and no torching or siphoning occurred.

text: The flight crew of a King Air reported a ground conflict with a Cirrus while landing at a non-towered airport. The Cirrus pilot was holding in an area very close to the runway, making it an unsafe condition.
rewrite: The King Air crew reported a ground conflict with a Cirrus during landing at a non-towered airport. The Cirrus was holding near the runway, creating an unsafe condition. The situation was exacerbated by the lack of tower control and visual cues, increasing the risk of a collision.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: EMB-145 Captain reported he was concerned with the slow response of ground personnel while parking with a medical issue in the cabin.
rewrite: EMB-145 Captain reported concern over delayed ground personnel response while parking, citing a medical issue in the cabin. The captain requested immediate assistance, noting the need for expedited handling due to the passenger's condition. Ground crew response was slower than expected, impacting the parking procedure.

text: Airline Flight Attendant reported having a gate agent commence passenger boarding before the required preflight safety checks were complete.
rewrite: Gate agent initiated passenger boarding prior to completion of required preflight safety checks, as reported by an airline flight attendant. The incident occurred during the predeparture phase, with no mention of urgency or special emergency conditions. The flight attendant noted the discrepancy but did not indicate any immediate safety threat or crew intervention.

text: The pilot of a C172 reported an NMAC with a helicopter during takeoff at night. The Tower had advised that the helicopter would be no factor, but the reporter disagreed.
rewrite: During takeoff at night, the C172 pilot reported an NMAC with a helicopter. Tower had advised the helicopter would be no factor, but the pilot disagreed, indicating a potential conflict during the takeoff roll.

text: G-IV flight crew reported diverting to a nearby alternate after a malfunctioning cargo door seal led to a loss of cabin pressure.
rewrite: A G-IV flight crew diverted to a nearby alternate aerodrome due to a malfunctioning cargo door seal resulting in a loss of cabin pressure. The crew initiated an emergency descent and communicated the situation to ATC. They requested an alternate aerodrome and proceeded to land at the nearest suitable airport.

text: After breaking out at 1,400 feet on the RNAV Y 13C at MDW, a Captain discovered that the PAPI lights were not operational, a requirement to shoot the approach during night time, and elects to continue to landing. The Tower indicates the PAPI's are NOTAMed out, but this proves not to be true. All approaches to Runways 13C and 4R at MDW require VGSI for night landings.
rewrite: After breaking out at 1,400 feet on the RNAV Y 13C approach at MDW, the Captain noted the PAPI lights were not operational, a requirement for night landings. The Tower confirmed the PAPIs were NOTAMed out, but this proved false. All approaches to Runways 13C and 4R require VGSI for night operations.

text: King Air 90 Captain reported that while under the guidance of a Marshaller his wingtip struck the tail boom of a helicopter that was parked in a dark area of the ramp.
rewrite: While taxiing under marshaller guidance, the King Air 90 captain's wingtip struck the tail boom of a parked helicopter on a dark ramp area. The incident occurred on the movement area, and the helicopter was positioned on a helipad. No prior clearance or communication with ATC was mentioned regarding the helicopter's position.

text: A PA-28 pilot reported losing directional control during rollout after landing in a crosswind.
rewrite: A PA-28 pilot reported losing directional control during rollout after landing in a crosswind. The pilot attempted to correct the drift but was unable to maintain alignment with the runway. The crosswind component exceeded the aircraft's handling capabilities during the landing rollout.

text: A B737 flight crew became distracted by a bird flock during takeoff roll. The flap handle may have been used to prop up the First Officer for better view resulting in movement of handle to flaps up.
rewrite: A B737 flight crew became distracted by a bird flock during takeoff roll. The flap handle may have been inadvertently moved to the up position, possibly to prop up the First Officer for a better view. This action resulted in an unintended flaps-up configuration.

text: HS125 Captain reported an NMAC on arrival into RYY.
rewrite: HS125 Captain reported an NMAC on arrival into RYY. The pilot observed another aircraft in proximity during the arrival phase. The report was made as the aircraft was establishing the approach to RYY.

text: A Dash-8 First Officer reported experiencing a main gear door warning light on climbout. Additionally, a cabin pressurization warning light illuminated. The first event was a mechanical issue and the second was crew induced.
rewrite: A Dash-8 First Officer reported a main gear door warning light illuminated during climbout, indicating a mechanical issue. A cabin pressurization warning light also activated, which the crew determined was crew-induced. Both events occurred during the initial climb phase.

text: The pilot of a C402 reported severe turbulence that resulted in a momentary loss of control and injury to one passenger.
rewrite: The pilot of a C402 encountered severe turbulence during cruise, leading to a momentary loss of control and injury to one passenger. The aircraft experienced a flyaway condition, with the pilot unable to regain command. The turbulence was intense enough to cause a loss of control, resulting in passenger injury.

text: An NCT TRACON Controller reported on a departing aircraft that flew straight out instead of turning as cleared on the LOUPE SID from SJC. The aircraft flew into adjacent sectors and the Departure Controller did not make a point out of the aircraft to one of those sectors.
rewrite: An NCT TRACON controller reported a departing aircraft that failed to turn as cleared on the LOUPE SID from SJC, instead flying straight out. The aircraft entered adjacent sectors without establishing a common point with the Departure Controller, who did not make a point out to one of those sectors. The departure path conflicted with the arrival window, causing potential separation issues.

text: A Pilatus PC12 pilot reported taking off with the tow bar still attached to the nose gear and upon gear retraction the nose gear would not lock up. The pilot reported he set up for a retracted nose gear landing, during the flare the nose gear locked down and the tow bar come off with runway contact. Gear was swung and an ultrasound inspection performed, no damage was found. Aircraft returned to service.
rewrite: A Pilatus PC12 pilot reported taking off with the tow bar still attached to the nose gear. During gear retraction, the nose gear failed to lock. The pilot configured for a retracted gear landing, but during the flare, the nose gear locked down, causing the tow bar to detach and result in runway contact. No damage was found after gear swing and ultrasound inspection; the aircraft was returned to service.
context: BRAKING ACTION (GOOD, GOOD TO MEDIUM, MEDIUM, MEDIUM TO POOR, POOR, OR NIL)

text: Air carrier flight crew reported being cleared to cross Runway 25R at LAX, but made an incorrect turn and ended up on the runway. They exited at the next intersection.
rewrite: Air carrier flight crew reported being cleared to cross Runway 25R at LAX, but made an incorrect turn and ended up on the runway. They exited at the next intersection, indicating they were clear of the runway after crossing. The crew did not follow the cleared route and deviated onto the active runway surface.

text: Beech 23 pilot reported a conflict with an aircraft on the runway while landing at a non-Towered airport. A go-around was initiated at approximately 200 feet AGL.
rewrite: A Beech 23 pilot reported an aircraft conflict on the runway during landing at a non-towered airport. The pilot initiated a go-around at approximately 200 feet AGL to avoid the conflicting traffic. No prior ATC coordination was required as the airport was non-towered.

text: Air Carrier First Officer reported that an unruly passenger disrupted the cabin shortly before landing.
rewrite: A first officer on an air carrier flight reported an unruly passenger causing disruption in the cabin shortly before landing, affecting the crew's ability to conduct a normal pre-landing briefing. The incident occurred during the approach phase, with the passenger refusing to comply with crew instructions and creating a safety concern. The crew requested assistance from the flight attendants to manage the situation.

text: B777 flight crew reported an unintentional cycling of the right engine fuel control switch during taxi in to the gate. A short time later, ground personnel reported a small flame coming from the engine.
rewrite: During taxi to the gate, the B777 flight crew noted unintentional cycling of the right engine fuel control switch. Shortly afterward, ground personnel observed a small flame emanating from the engine, prompting an immediate shutdown and inspection.

text: DA-20 instructor pilot reported returning to the departure airport after the engine began to run rough and show a loss of oil pressure.
rewrite: DA-20 instructor pilot executed a round flight plan, returning to the departure airport after the engine began running rough and showed a loss of oil pressure, indicating a potential flameout condition. The pilot initiated emergency procedures and assessed the situation during the approach. No communications were lost, and the pilot maintained control throughout the event.

text: CRJ-200 Captain reported executing a low altitude go-around at CLT when the flight ballooned as a result of either a gust of wind or a wake turbulence encounter.
rewrite: CRJ-200 Captain executed a low altitude go-around at CLT after the flight ballooned, attributed to either a wind gust or wake turbulence. The pilot reported encountering an unexpected upward movement, consistent with either CLEAR AIR TURBULENCE or wake turbulence from a preceding aircraft. The maneuver was initiated to regain control and ensure safe altitude.

text: The Captain of a CRJ200 reported missing the notes on an electronic chart that made the clearance in conflict with the aircraft MEL restrictions.
rewrite: The Captain of a CRJ200 reported missing notes on an electronic chart, resulting in a clearance that conflicted with the aircraft's MEL restrictions. The pilot failed to note a restriction affecting the cleared procedure, leading to a potential conflict resolution issue. The situation required immediate attention to ensure compliance with both the clearance and MEL limitations.

text: The pilot of a C210 reported the loss of the alternator during climb on a missed approach in instrument conditions. A successful landing at the airport was completed.
rewrite: During climb on a missed approach in instrument conditions, the pilot of a C210 reported loss of the alternator. The pilot executed a successful landing at the airport. No alternate airport was required.

text: CRJ-700 flight crew reported an altitude overshoot resulted when the wrong altitude was entered into the MCP alert window. Crew cited workload and distractions as contributing.
rewrite: During climbout, the CRJ-700 crew entered an incorrect altitude in the MCP alert window, leading to an altitude overshoot. Workload and distractions were cited as contributing factors. The autopilot did not engage due to the incorrect entry.

text: B737 Captain reported returning to the departure airport when a master caution light indicated a slow loss of hydraulic fluid from the A system.
rewrite: A B737 captain initiated a return to the departure airport after a master caution light indicated a slow loss of hydraulic fluid from the A system. The pilot assessed the situation and decided to divert back to the departure airport for further evaluation. No communication issues were reported during the flight.

text: EMB-145 Captain reported returning to the departure airport after noting the EICAS message 'ELEC EMERG ABNORMAL.'
rewrite: EMB-145 Captain executed a ROUND flight plan after receiving an EICAS message indicating 'ELEC EMERG ABNORMAL,' prompting a return to the departure airport for further assessment. The pilot initiated a diversion without declaring an emergency, following standard procedures for electrical system anomalies. No acrobatic flight or terminal data link system involvement was noted during the event.

text: EMB145 First Officer refused to continue flying an aircraft with both ACARS and the FMC on MEL after being told it would be taken out of service after return to base on the basis of safety of flight issues.
rewrite: The EMB145 First Officer declined to proceed with the flight when both ACARS and the FMC were inoperative, citing safety concerns. The aircraft was scheduled to be taken out of service upon return to base due to MEL items. The decision was based on the potential risk to flight safety.

text: C172 flight instructor reported taking control from his student during landing, but the student keeps his feet on the brakes. By the time the instructor has full control of the aircraft there is insufficient runway remaining to stop or go around and the aircraft goes into the fence at the end of the runway.
rewrite: A C172 flight instructor took control from his student during landing, but the student kept his feet on the brakes. By the time the instructor had full control, there was insufficient runway remaining to stop or go around. The aircraft subsequently impacted the fence at the end of the runway.

text: Two maintenance technicians reported that while retracting the Main Landing Gear on a Bombardier CRJ200 for maintenance, with the MLG door disconnected, the bellcrank was out of the proper position causing the linkage to break and damage to the aircraft.
rewrite: Two maintenance technicians were retracting the Main Landing Gear on a Bombardier CRJ200 during maintenance when the MLG door was disconnected. The bellcrank was out of the proper position, leading to linkage failure and aircraft damage. The incident occurred while the gear was being retracted.

text: C172 Instructor reported a runway excursion during a cross-wind landing and regained control after aircraft slowed down.

rewrite: During an oceanic flight, the air carrier First Officer informed ATC that the Dispatcher had filed a flight plan routing the aircraft through known turbulence areas, which the crew had not been briefed on prior to departure. text: Air carrier flight crew reported they were cleared by SLC Ground to Runway 16L via Taxiways H, F, G. Because of their location on the air carrier apron, they mistook Taxiway E for F, but made the correct turn onto Taxiway G. Poor signage and complex taxiways were reported factors.

rewrite: An A330 flight crew encountered a fuel quantity anomaly during a trans-Atlantic flight, suggesting a potential fuel leak. rewrite: During the approach phase, the CRJ-200 First Officer experienced a stick shaker, indicating a loss of aerodynamic control. rewrite: A C172 pilot reported that search and rescue personnel were searching for them due to a filed arrival time delay caused by practice touch and goes conducted en route. rewrite: A B737 flight crew reported a light indication on the landing gear system, which was traced to a popped circuit breaker. The crew suspected the shoulder harness may have caused the breaker to trip. The issue occurred during the approach phase of the flight.

rewrite: An A300 flight crew executed a ROUND flight plan, returning to the departure airport after the Number 2 engine abruptly rolled back to idle during cruise. rewrite: An MD-11 flight crew reported difficulty understanding an Iranian controller's clearance, potentially leading to a missed crossing restriction during descent. rewrite: The flight crew of a B737 received a report of potential damage to the vertical stabilizer near the top. Following a maintenance inspection, the aircraft was removed from service due to the identified issue. No further details on the cause or extent of the damage were provided.

rewrite: A C210 pilot experienced engine failure during cruise and executed a successful off-field landing. The pilot declared an emergency and followed procedures for a forced landing. No injuries were reported, and the aircraft was undamaged.

rewrite: A C172 instructor pilot encountered a near mid-air collision (NMAC) with another Cessna in the vicinity of ELN VOR. rewrite: A Dash-8 captain diverted to an alternate airport following the failure of #1 pitot heat and #1 communication radio, rendering the aircraft unsuitable for continued approach and landing at the original destination. rewrite: The L30 TRACON controller lost separation because an aircraft failed to maintain visual separation while the controller was using FUSION radar. rewrite: An air carrier dispatcher reported that insufficient staffing led to an unacceptably high workload. rewrite: ZAU Center Controller reported a loss of separation as an aircraft was unable to comply with crossing restrictions. text: SoCal TRACON Controller reported a bad readback from a pilot which caused an instantaneous airspace violation.
rewrite: SoCal TRACON controller noted a bad readback from a pilot, leading to an immediate airspace deviation. The pilot failed to correctly acknowledge a clearance, resulting in an unauthorized entry into restricted airspace. The controller issued a correction and initiated procedures to re-establish separation.

text: GA pilot departing using CTAF procedures reported a NMAC with a vintage aircraft departing on an adjacent runway without announcing on CTAF.
rewrite: A general aviation pilot departing on a touch-and-go maneuver using CTAF procedures reported a near mid-air collision (NMAC) with a vintage aircraft that departed on an adjacent runway without announcing its intentions on the CTAF. text: A300 flight crew reported rejecting the takeoff and returning for maintenance after experiencing anomalies affecting both generators. The problem was traced to water in the avionics compartment.
rewrite: An A300 flight crew rejected takeoff due to anomalies affecting both generators. The issue was later identified as water in the avionics compartment, prompting a return to base for maintenance. The crew initiated a go-around and diverted to the nearest suitable airport for inspection.

text: Guam Center Controller reported a possible loss of separation between two aircraft due to lack of oversight and high workload environment as a result of minimal staffing.
rewrite: Guam Center Controller noted a potential loss of separation between two aircraft caused by insufficient oversight and elevated workload stemming from reduced staffing levels. The controller's ability to manage traffic was compromised, increasing the risk of mid-air conflict. The situation highlights challenges in maintaining safe separation under resource-constrained conditions.
context: EN ROUTE AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL SERVICES

text: B737 First Officer reported a shiny object passed very close to the right engine while level at 15000 ft during an EWR departure.
rewrite: During the EWR departure, the B737 First Officer observed a shiny object pass very close to the right engine while the aircraft was level at 15,000 ft. The object was noted to be near the engine nacelle, but no immediate engine anomalies were reported. The pilot did not initiate any evasive action or communicate the incident to ATC.

text: CRJ-200 First Officer reported they failed to complete power down checklist resulting in the engine operating with no flight crew onboard.
rewrite: A CRJ-200 First Officer reported they did not complete the power down checklist, leading to the engine remaining operational while no flight crew was onboard. The failure to follow the checklist resulted in the engine continuing to run unattended. This incident highlights a critical procedural lapse during the power down phase.

text: Sea Rey LSX pilot reported the aircraft partially sank after taking on water related to the failure of the rubber hull boots.
rewrite: A Sea Rey LSX pilot reported the aircraft partially sank after taking on water due to the failure of the rubber hull boots, which allowed water ingress during operations on a SEA LANE. The incident occurred while the aircraft was operating on water, leading to partial submersion and requiring immediate action to prevent further damage.

text: Corporate Jet flight crew reported receiving conflicting ATC instructions on the OOSHN4 arrival into BOS.
rewrite: Corporate Jet flight crew received conflicting ATC instructions during the OOSHN4 arrival into BOS. The crew reported receiving conflicting clearances, leading to confusion during the approach phase. The conflicting instructions affected their ability to execute the approach safely and efficiently.

text: R44 Instructor reported a precautionary landing in a field due to power fluctuations.
rewrite: An R44 instructor executed a precautionary landing in a field after experiencing power fluctuations during flight. The instructor noted the power issues and decided to land to ensure safety. No specific cause was identified, but the landing area was suitable for the aircraft.

text: Air Traffic Controller reported the need to vector an aircraft off the final approach course to avoid fast moving VFR traffic in the area of Boeing Field .
rewrite: The air traffic controller vectored the aircraft off the final approach course to avoid fast-moving VFR traffic near Boeing Field. The controller used a surveillance approach procedure, providing altitude instructions based on radar position. The aircraft was cleared to the outer fix before being vectored to the approach gate.

text: A320 Captain reported a NMAC with a glider west of DEN at 16,000 feet.
rewrite: A320 Captain reported a near mid-air collision (NMAC) with a glider west of Denver (DEN) at 16,000 feet during cruise. The glider was operating in the North Pacific route system and was flying at a lower altitude. The captain initiated a climb to avoid the potential conflict.

text: GA flight instructor reported a near mid air collision with another aircraft while turning onto final approach at Joplin Regional Airport.
rewrite: A GA flight instructor was turning onto final approach at Joplin Regional Airport when a near mid-air collision occurred with another aircraft. The instructor was on the final approach course, having completed a procedure turn inbound, and was establishing position for landing. The other aircraft was also in the vicinity, resulting in a close encounter.

text: PA-25 pilot reported fuel exhaustion and an off airport landing in an open field during glider tow operations.
rewrite: During glider tow operations, a PA-25 pilot declared fuel exhaustion and executed an off-airport landing in an open field. The pilot reported fuel remaining as approximately zero minutes, leading to an emergency landing away from the designated landing area. The incident occurred during the final approach phase of the tow flight.

text: A Maintenance Inspector reported that the front engine mounts did not have washers installed.
rewrite: A Maintenance Inspector noted that the front engine mounts were missing washers, which could affect engine installation and potentially lead to a flameout during flight. The issue was identified during a routine inspection, and the absence of washers may compromise the structural integrity of the engine mounts.

text: ZAB Developmental Controller reported issuing a departure clearance through the FSS which did not ensure terrain clearance.
rewrite: ZAB Developmental Controller issued a departure clearance via FSS without ensuring terrain clearance. The clearance lacked appropriate terrain clearance minimum altitude. The controller failed to verify terrain clearance requirements during the DCL application process.

text: CRJ-700 flight crew reported that their aircraft started rolling forward at the gate when ramp personnel removed the chocks without informing the flight crew.
rewrite: During taxi-out, ramp personnel removed chocks from a CRJ-700 without notifying the flight crew, causing the aircraft to begin rolling forward at the gate. The pilot-in-command immediately took action to stop the movement. The incident occurred while the aircraft was stationary on the ramp.

text: Hawkwer 4000 Captain reported taking evasive action after an NMAC on downwind at BED airport.
rewrite: Hawkwer 4000 Captain took evasive action following an NMAC on downwind leg at BED airport. The incident occurred during the traffic pattern, specifically on the downwind leg. The pilot reported an unauthorized UAS in the vicinity, prompting immediate evasive maneuvers.

text: Air carrier flight crew reported difficulty in executing an RNAV approach using aircraft systems automation which resulted in going below glideslope mid-approach at SDF.
rewrite: During an RNAV approach, the flight crew encountered difficulty with aircraft systems automation, leading to a descent below the glideslope mid-approach at the SDF. The incident occurred during the intermediate segment of the approach.

text: B737 flight crew reported FMC route data was missing two fixes on their assigned departure SKYL8 from OAK.
rewrite: A B737 flight crew reported that their FMC route data was missing two fixes on the assigned departure SKYL8 from OAK, leading to an off-course situation. text: A Hawker 4000 Captain reported a yaw damper system failure and a rudder fault with associated autopilot disconnect and instability inflight while overwater at FL400. The crew regained control, reversed course, and returned to the departure airport.
rewrite: A Hawker 4000 captain reported a yaw damper system failure and rudder fault, resulting in autopilot disconnection and aircraft instability while overwater at FL400. text: CRJ200 flight crew reported being informed by ATC that they were off course. They informed the crew that there was reported GPS signal jamming in the area.
rewrite: CRJ200 flight crew advised ATC they were off course. ATC confirmed GPS signal jamming in the area, affecting navigation. Crew requested further instructions due to loss of position information.

text: CE560 Captain reported a near miss with a UAV.
rewrite: CE560 Captain reported a near miss with a UAV during the approach phase. text: Air carrier Captain reported sighting 2 UAVs while conducting an approach at LGA. The event was reported to ATC, however no evasive action was taken.
rewrite: Air carrier Captain observed two UAVs during approach to LGA. The pilot reported the sighting to ATC, but no evasive action was initiated. No disruption to traffic or runway changes occurred.

text: A300 flight crew reported a rejected takeoff due to no airspeed indication, after failing to ensure the pitot covers were removed during preflight.
rewrite: During a rejected takeoff, the A300 flight crew experienced no airspeed indication, resulting in a go-around. text: B747 First Officer reported a course deviation resulted when the ANC 07R localizer signal displayed anomalies. Reporter stated he has seen this issue in the past.
rewrite: A B747 First Officer reported a course deviation due to anomalies in the ANC 07R localizer signal. text: Student pilot reported the aircraft became unstable during a solo landing that resulted in the propeller striking the runway surface.
rewrite: Student pilot conducted a solo landing when the aircraft became unstable, resulting in the propeller contacting the runway surface. The incident occurred during the final approach phase. No prior indication of instability was reported.

text: IAH Ramp Agent reported the ramp has a slope which caused an aircraft to drag its attached tug when the brakes were released.
rewrite: A ramp agent at IAH reported that the ramp's slope caused an aircraft to drag its attached tug when the brakes were released, resulting in a nonmovement area incident during ramp operations. text: Airbus A319 flight crew reported that due to extreme turbulence they were unable to maintain altitude or speed.
rewrite: Airbus A319 crew encountered extreme turbulence, preventing them from maintaining altitude or speed. rewrite: During departure, the B737 Captain and First Officer exceeded a published speed restriction after reconfiguring their EFB display, inadvertently hiding the airspeed restriction from view. text: EMB-175 Captain reported they initiated a go-around below 1,000 feet due to severe weather and a windshear warning.
rewrite: EMB-175 captain initiated a go-around below 1,000 feet due to severe weather and a windshear warning.
